== README ==
# gamarr

**gamarr** finds great games and puts them in your library — no browsing,
no manual searches, no cleanup. A configurable pipeline scrapes Metacritic
for critically-acclaimed releases, filters out unwanted genres and keywords,
matches titles against FitGirl repacks and FreeGOG, and delivers
torrents to qBittorrent. Once downloads complete, a post-processing thread
SHA-256-verifies and copies each game to your library with customizable path
templates, then cleans up source torrents. Runs as a daemon so your library
stays fresh without lifting a finger.

## Features

- **Two-phase score verification** — browse pages use internal Metacritic
  metrics (not real 0–100 scores) to build a candidate pool quickly.
  Browse scores are on a completely different scale (e.g. 1478, 1931) and
  **always pass** the configured thresholds — the real 0–100 score
  filtering only happens during the detail-page verification step.
  This avoids hundreds of slow HTTP requests while keeping score accuracy.
- **Genre-based rejection** — exclude games by genre using case-insensitive
  substring matching (e.g. `["RPG"]` rejects "Action RPG", "JRPG", etc.).
- **Keyword-based filtering** — reject games whose titles or FitGirl page
  description contain specific keywords.
- **Relative date cutoff** — set a look-back window in weeks instead of
  maintaining a static date (e.g. `max_pages: 500` for ~21 months of releases).
- **Re-verification with expiry** — games whose real Metacritic detail
  page scores don't match the browse page scores are kept in a pending queue
  for re-verification until they expire (`max_queue_days`). Once scores pass
  thresholds, a fresh expiry window begins for the FitGirl-matching phase.
- **Two-phase pending expiry** — games awaiting score review expire after
  `max_queue_days` (under metacritic thresholds). Once scores pass, a fresh
  expiry window (`download_sites.fitgirl.max_queue_days`) starts for the
  FitGirl-matching phase. Set either value to `0` for indefinite pending.
- **Multiple download sources** — supports FreeGOGPCGames (A-Z list-based)
  and FitGirl repacks (sitemap-based). Sources are configured as an ordered
  list — position determines priority, and the first source with a match
  delivers the torrent.
- **Source priority** — if a game is available on multiple sources, the
  highest-priority source in the config list is used. Games that don't match
  any source remain in the pending queue.
- **Database deduplication** — every processed game is recorded in SQLite;
  previously processed titles are never re-processed.
- **Configurable cache TTLs** — Metacritic scores and browse pages are cached
  with independent TTLs to reduce HTTP requests.
- **Notifications** — sends alerts via any
  [apprise](https://github.com/caronc/apprise)-compatible service (ntfy,
  Discord, Telegram, email, and more).
- **Schedule mode** — runs as a scheduled background process with separate
  intervals for acquisition and post-processing, or in foreground mode for
  single-pass execution.
- **Automatic config migration** — upgrades the YAML config schema
  automatically on startup when new fields are added.
- **Post-processing** — a background thread polls qBittorrent for completed
  downloads, copies them to a configurable library path with SHA-256
  verification, and cleans up source torrents after seeding goals are met.
  Torrents whose metadata has not been fetched yet (a paused magnet holds no
  files) are not complete: they are skipped quietly and reported once per cycle
  in the summary line (`N downloading, M awaiting metadata`), never as a copy
  failure.

== SPEC head -40 ==
# Design: sort_order `criticscore`/`userscore` and critic-threshold rename

Date: 2026-08-31
Status: Approved

## Goal

1. Add a third `sort_order` value, `userscore`, which browses Metacritic
   in user-score order.
2. Rename `sort_order: metascore` to `sort_order: criticscore` so the
   values read clearly as `new`, `criticscore`, `userscore`.
3. For naming consistency, also rename the critic-threshold keys:
   `min_metascore` → `min_criticscore`,
   `min_metascore_reviews` → `min_criticscore_reviews`.

## Decisions (user-approved)

- **Migration strategy: auto-migrate the YAML file in place.** On first
  load after upgrade, gamarr rewrites the user's `gamarr.yml` with the
  new key names (matching the existing config-version migration
  pattern). No manual user action required.
- **`userscore` is sort-only.** The browse phase only changes candidate
  discovery ORDER; all score thresholding still happens at detail-page
  verification. The two-phase score model is unchanged.
- The rename is total: the legacy `metascore` spellings are not valid
  config values after migration.

## Current mechanics (verified)

- `MetacriticPlatformConfig.sort_order: Literal["new", "metascore"] = "new"`
  (config.py), mirrored in `pipeline.py` (`run_acquisition`,
  `AcquisitionConfig`).
- The sort value is interpolated directly into the Metacritic browse URL:
  `https://www.metacritic.com/browse/game/{platform}/all/{year_str}/{sort_order}/`.
  Live check: the slugs `new`, `metascore`, and `userscore` all return
  HTTP 200 with the expected Nuxt browse-page structure.
- `new` mode scans per-year with the `max_pages` budget; `metascore`
  uses the else-branch (no year dimension, `year=0` sentinel, single
  budget stream).
- A detected sort-order change clears the metacritic cache and resets

content.text:
## Context synthesis — gamarr

🖥️ Harness: pi.

- **What it is:** `gamarr` (`/data/gamarr`, branch `main`, v3.2.5, single Python 3.12/uv package `src/gamarr`) — a daemon that scrapes Metacritic for critically-acclaimed releases, filters genre/keyword rejects, matches titles against FitGirl/FreeGOG, sends torrents to qBittorrent, then SHA-256-verifies and copies completed downloads into a templated library path. Pending queues expire via `max_queue_days`; config is YAML (`gamarr.yml`) with automatic in-place schema migration on startup.

- **The three keys the request touches are documented in three distinct places in `README.md`:** `max_pages` (line 178, default `500`, "total browse page depth budget", `0` = unlimited), `max_cycle_pages` (line 179, default `0`, per-cycle pacing), and `cache_pages_hours` (line 184, default `6`, Metacritic browse-page cache). Critical nuance: `cache_pages_hours` also appears under the **download-source** section (line 164, default `6`) where it caches the FitGirl **source index**, not pages — so a rename to `cache_hours` collides across two different config owners, while the FitGirl one was never page-based to begin with. Keys also appear in README examples (lines 147, 153) and narrative text (lines 25, 304-311, 434).

- **Page budget mechanics are baked into the pipeline, not just the config:** browsing advances a persistent page cursor across cycles, resets to page 1 when the `max_pages` budget is exhausted, and `max_cycle_pages` caps pages per cycle. A prior change (`436bd18 feat!: remove search_mode, unify browse loop with max_pages budget`) made the browse loop a single unified page-budget stream; `113ffff fix: drain newest year first and scope browse pages by release year` then layered per-year scoping on top. Any date-based replacement must interact with that per-year scan order and the stored cursor, not just swap a scalar.

- **Established precedent for exactly this kind of rename:** commit `b62ac25 feat: add userscore sort order and rename critic-score config keys` (spec `docs/agent/specs/2026-08-31-sort-order-userscore-design.md`, plan `docs/agent/plans/2026-08-31-sort-order-userscore.md`) did a total key rename (`min_metascore` → `min_criticscore`) via the user-approved strategy of **auto-migrating `gamarr.yml` in place** — a new `_migrate_*` function rewrites the raw YAML dict, `load_config` writes back and bumps `config_version` once, and legacy spellings are invalid afterwards. That spec/plan pair also establishes the file map a rename must cover: `config.py`, `pipeline.py`, `scheduler.py` (`_build_kwargs`), `README.md`, and four test modules including `tests/unit/test_readme_accuracy.py`.

- **`tests/unit/test_readme_accuracy.py` is a hard constraint on README edits:** it parses the config tables as exactly three columns (`Key | Description | Default`) and asserts README defaults against code. Adding a valid-values column, or renaming a key without updating that test, breaks the suite.

- **A prior look-back-window concept already exists and was superseded:** README feature bullet line 25 advertises "Relative date cutoff — set a look-back window in weeks ... (e.g. `max_pages: 500` for ~21 months of releases)", and legacy plans include `2026-06-08-cutoff-weeks.md`, `2026-06-12-max-cycle-weeks.md`, `2026-06-10-age-recheck-weeks.md`. So the repo already has cutoff/date machinery and a documented history of weeks-based cutoffs being replaced by page budgets — the requested change is a partial return to a date concept, and that earlier date/cutoff code is the most likely reuse surface.

- **Immediately prior session (2026-11-06, same day):** you asked to make the README list *valid values* for CLI/config options rather than just descriptions and defaults. The session traced the source and found **there is no `--platform` CLI flag** (platform is a config key), that only `--log-level` and `--clear-cache` are truly enumerated, and that the 3-column README parser blocks a naive new column — then it stopped at an `ask_user_question` about scope and never completed. No README change landed, so this rename and that unfinished README-valid-values work touch the same tables.

- **Current state / hygiene:** working tree is on `main` at `1f09be0 chore: bump version to 3.2.5` with the last few commits being fixes to duplicate-torrent/copy-failure reporting and year-scoped browsing. `docs/agent/` contains only the one spec and one plan above — **no `docs/agent/reviews/` directory exists, so there are no residual or deferred review ledgers** holding known defects for this repo.

`Project context status: loaded.`

Follow the Create Spec skill. Explore project context by checking files, docs, and recent commits. Ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once the design is clear, present it formally and get user approval.

**Use `ask_user_question` to present each question** — one at a time. Do NOT dump all questions in prose. Each question must use the tool so the chain waits for the user's answer.

Do NOT write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until the design is approved. This step is design only.

Context: so at present gamarr uses page counts to denote how far to backlog, this is a bit crap to be honest, as pages means nothing to a human, and in fact a single page can be full of games with zero score so pages does not equal games ot be reviewed!. so i want to switch from using pages ot using dates, dates are known to humans and are easy to work with, so lets switch the following over to use dates:- max_pages becomes max_date in the format of YYYYMM, max_cycle_pages becomes max_cycle_months in the digit format XX, cache_pages_hours becomes simply cache_hours as we are no longer ocunting things based on pages and gthis cache_pages_hours makes no sense any more, i know there will be lots of quesitons, ask them all!.

                    result.append(val)
                else:
                    result.append({"name": key})
        return result

content.text:
I've explored the mechanics. Key findings that shape the design:

- `max_pages` is not just a knob — it drives a **year range** (`years_back = ceil(max_pages / 52)`), a **durable per-year page cursor** (`last_scanned_page`), a **shared `total_scanned` budget** across years, and a **reset-to-page-1 when exhausted** cycle. Nothing about that is human-readable, and README's "500 pages ≈ 21 months" disagrees with the code's `ceil(500/52)` = **10 years**.
- A date mechanism **already exists and is unused**: `scan_recent_games(cutoff_date=...)` + `_page_is_before_cutoff()`, but `pipeline.py` always passes `cutoff_date=None`.
- `cache_pages_hours` exists on **two different models** — `MetacriticPlatformConfig` (browse-page cache) and `SourceConfigEntry` (FitGirl/FreeGOG sitemap cache) — so the rename touches both owners.
- Established precedent: `b62ac25` renamed config keys with in-place YAML auto-migration + `config_version` bump. This change should ride the same path.

Question 1 of several:

options.description: `max_date: 202401` = sweep every month back to (and including) January 2024, newest first. Inside the boundary year the scan stops as soon as a page's games are all older than 2024-01 — using the cutoff_date early-stop that already exists in metacritic.py but is currently never passed. Answers 'how far back do I review?' in the same units a human thinks in, and stops exactly where you said.

Simplest change (pure year-range maths, no mid-year stop), but it can overshoot by up to 11 months of releases you did not ask for — which is the same class of imprecision you are complaining about with pages.

Keeps page traversal unlimited during a sweep and does the work anyway, then throws it away — worst of both worlds on HTTP budget, but makes max_date a strict 'only games released on/after this month' rule.

content.text:
Let me clear that up — you're right that date mode needs exactly **two** numbers from you:

| Date mode (`sort_order: new` + `max_date` set) | Key |
| --- | --- |
| Where to stop (absolute floor) | `max_date` |
| How much progress per cycle | `max_cycle_months` |

Nothing else is conceptually needed. `max_cycle_pages` drops out of date mode entirely (that answers Q7 — it's inert there).

The **only** remaining wrinkle is a guard, and it exists for a mechanical reason, not a conceptual one: "2 months of backlog" is not a fixed amount of work. Two quiet months might be 9 pages; two busy release months can be 300+. On a cold cache that can exceed `acquisition_timeout_mins: 25`, which aborts the cycle mid-sweep. So *something* has to cap pages fetched per cycle. That's the only open question:

content.text:
Two useful facts: `scan_state.last_cutoff_date` (TEXT) already exists and is **unused by the pipeline** (only its own DB methods and tests reference it), and `scan_state` already has additive `ALTER TABLE` migration precedent. `backlog_progress` keeps per-year page cursors, which stay as the resume mechanism.

That gives one real architectural fork — where the month "progress" lives:

**A. Span-from-cursor, no new state** — each cycle scans from wherever the year cursors are and stops once the games it has seen span `max_cycle_months` months (first page whose release dates reach past the target). Nothing persisted beyond today's page cursors; nothing to invalidate when you change `max_date`/`max_cycle_months`.

**B. Durable frontier in the unused `last_cutoff_date` column** — store `"YYYY-MM"` of the oldest month reached; target = frontier − months, clamped to `max_date`. Gives an exact "sweeping 2024-01 → 2026-11, now at 2024-03" progress line, but adds stale-state risk: changing `max_date` must invalidate the stored frontier.

**C. New `frontier_month` column** — same as B with an honest name, plus an `ALTER TABLE` migration (precedent exists at `database.py:265-270`).

I recommend **A**: it satisfies "each cycle advances N months" without new persistence, and the only reporting loss is a cosmetic progress line that can instead say "reached 2024-03 (floor 2024-01)".

The cycle measures the span of release dates it has actually walked: it stops at the first page whose games reach past (first page of cycle - max_cycle_months), clamped so it never crosses max_date. Per-year page cursors remain the only persisted state, so changing max_date or max_cycle_months can never leave a stale frontier behind. Progress logging reports the oldest month this cycle reached plus the configured floor.

content.text:
All decisions are locked. Here is the design — four sections; tell me what to change and I'll revise before writing the spec.

---

## 1. Goal and scope

**Problem:** the backlog cutoff is expressed as `max_pages: 500`, which no human can interpret, and page count does not equal games reviewed (a page of zero-score games costs one page and yields nothing).

**Goal:** let the cutoff be stated as a **date**, without breaking score-ordered browsing, which structurally cannot use dates (its browse list is score-ordered across all years, so a page mixes 2015 and 2025 titles).

**Approach: add, don't replace.**

| Mode | Condition | Bound | Pace | Inert |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Date mode** | `max_date` != 0 **and** `sort_order: new` | `max_date` (absolute month floor) | `max_cycle_months` | `max_pages`, `max_cycle_pages` |
| **Page mode** | anything else | `max_pages` (exactly as today) | `max_cycle_pages` (exactly as today) | `max_date`, `max_cycle_months` |

`max_date` is the precedence key: setting it switches `sort_order: new` to dates. In score modes both date keys are inert and a single INFO line says so per cycle. In date mode `max_cycle_pages` is inert and `max_pages` is inert too (no page guard, per your decision).

**Out of scope:** pending-queue expiry (`max_queue_days`) is unchanged; queue members are not retro-filtered by `max_date`.

---

## 2. Config surface

```yaml
review_sites:
  metacritic:
    platform_overrides:
      pc:
        max_date: 0            # 0 = disabled (page mode). YYYYMM enables date mode.
        max_cycle_months: 0    # 0 = no month pacing; sweep to max_date, watchdog permitting.
        max_pages: 500         # page mode bound only
        max_cycle_pages: 0     # page mode pace only
        cache_hours: 6         # renamed from cache_pages_hours
download_sites:
  - fitgirl:
      cache_hours: 6          # renamed from cache_pages_hours
  - freegog:
      cache_hours: 6          # renamed from cache_pages_hours
```

- `max_date: int = 0`. Valid: `0` or a 6-digit `YYYYMM` with month `01`–`12` (`202401`). Anything else (`2024`, `202413`, `2024-01`) is a config error with the message *"max_date must be 0 (disabled) or YYYYMM with month 01-12, e.g. 202401"*.
- `max_cycle_months: int = 0`, `ge=0`. `0` = no month pacing.
- `max_date` later than the current month → warning + clamp to the current month (nothing to sweep otherwise, and failing outright would be hostile).
- Both keys live in `MetacriticPlatformConfig`, so per-platform overrides work like every other key.
- **Migration:** `cache_pages_hours` → `cache_hours` in all three locations via one new `_migrate_cache_pages_hours_to_cache_hours()`, values preserved, `config_version` bumped, ridden by the existing `migrated=True` write-back. No value conversion for `max_date`/`max_cycle_months` — they default to `0`, so upgrading changes nobody's behaviour.

---

## 3. Scan algorithm (date mode)

```
floor_month   = max_date                              # absolute, never crossed
year_range    = current_year down to max_date // 100
cycle_start   = first page fetched this cycle
target_month  = cycle_start_month - max_cycle_months  # clamped >= floor_month
              (max_cycle_months == 0 -> target = floor_month)

for year in year_range (newest first):
    resume from backlog_progress[year].last_scanned_page + 1
    scan pages, passing cutoff_date = YYYY-MM-01 of max(floor_month, target_month)
    stop this cycle when a page's games are all older than target_month
    persist last_scanned_page only for pages really fetched   (unchanged)
```

- **Reuses existing machinery:** `scan_recent_games(cutoff_date=...)` + `_page_is_before_cutoff()` already implement "stop when every game on this page predates the cutoff" — `pipeline.py` currently always passes `None`. Date mode passes a real value. No change to `metacritic.py` scan logic beyond what exists.
- **No page budget arithmetic in date mode.** `total_scanned` / `sum_scanned_pages` and the "budget exhausted → reset to page 1" branch do not run; the static floor replaces them entirely. Page-mode behaviour is untouched.
- **No new database state.** Per-year `backlog_progress` cursors are the only persistence; the month target is derived from the cycle's own pages, so changing `max_date` or `max_cycle_months` can never leave a stale frontier behind.
- **Drain/restart:** reaching the floor counts as drained (existing `_recent_games_exhausted` probe path, floor-clamped) → `reset_progress()` so the next sweep starts at the newest year and picks up new releases.
- **Progress logging:** date mode replaces `"N of 500 pages (x%)"` with `"Backlog: reached 2025-11 (floor 2024-01, year 2025 page 12)"`. Page mode keeps its current line.

---

## 4. Error handling, testing, files

**Error handling:** fetch failure in a year still marks `fetch_failed`, leaves the cursor untouched, and never counts as drained (existing rules preserved). Cancellation returns partial results and keeps fetched-page cursors. A cycle aborted by `acquisition_timeout_mins` loses no progress because cursors advance per page fetched. `max_cycle_months` larger than the span to the floor simply stops at the floor.

**New helpers:** month arithmetic (`_subtract_months(yyyymm, n)`, `_month_of(release_date)`) in `utils.py`, unit-tested in isolation — no date maths inlined into `pipeline.py`.

**Tests:**
- `test_config.py` — default `0`s, `YYYYMM` validation accept/reject table, future-clamp warning, cache-key migration in all three locations, per-platform override.
- `test_pipeline.py` — mode resolution matrix (4 combinations of `max_date` set/unset × `new`/score), month-span stop, clamp at floor, `max_cycle_pages`/`max_pages` inert in date mode, no budget-reset in date mode, drain-reset at floor.
- `test_scheduler.py` — `_build_kwargs` passes the new keys and the renamed cache key.
- `test_readme_accuracy.py` — renamed rows/defaults; new rows for `max_date`/`max_cycle_months`.
- `test_metacritic.py` — cutoff pass-through stops mid-year (largely covers existing code).
- `test_database.py` — unchanged.

**Files:** `src/gamarr/config.py`, `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`, `src/gamarr/scheduler.py`, `src/gamarr/utils.py` (+ the four test modules), `README.md`. `src/gamarr/metacritic.py` and `src/gamarr/database.py` need no changes — worth stating explicitly in the spec.

## Design

### 1. Config surface (`src/gamarr/config.py`)

- `sort_order: Literal["new", "criticscore", "userscore"] = "new"`.
- Rename fields: `min_criticscore: int = 75`,
  `min_criticscore_reviews: int = 10`.
- `load_config()` gains a legacy-key mapping pass that runs before
  pydantic validation:
  - `metascore` → `criticscore` (under
    `review_sites.metacritic.platform_overrides.<platform>`),
  - `min_metascore` → `min_criticscore`,
  - `min_metascore_reviews` → `min_criticscore_reviews`.
- If any legacy key was present, rewrite `gamarr.yml` in place with the
  new names. The rewrite is naturally one-time: after it, the legacy
  keys no longer exist, so later loads find nothing to migrate (the
  project's migrations are key-presence-driven, not version-marker
  driven). Log an INFO line naming the migrated keys (same tone as the
  existing migration logs). After rewriting, reload the migrated dict so
  the rest of startup sees only new spellings.

### 2. Pipeline and metacritic (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py`, `src/gamarr/metacritic.py`)

- Widen the `sort_order` Literals in `run_acquisition` and
  `AcquisitionConfig` to `["new", "criticscore", "userscore"]`.
- `MetacriticClient` needs no change: the value is passed straight into
  the URL slug, and `userscore` is a valid slug.
- `userscore` takes the existing else-branch (no per-year dimension,
  `year=0`, single `max_pages` budget stream) — identical flow to
  `criticscore`. Only `new` keeps per-year scanning.
- Sort-change detection stays string-based. Upgrading a `metascore`
  install to `criticscore` therefore triggers a ONE-TIME cache clear and
  browse-progress reset (the progress dimension key changes). This is
  accepted: it is a correctness-preserving reset, not data loss.

### 3. Behavior

- `sort_order` only changes discovery order. `min_criticscore`,
  `min_criticscore_reviews`, `min_user_score`, `min_user_reviews`
  filtering remains at detail-page verification. The README's
  two-phase-score caveats remain accurate.

### 4. Docs and tests

- README config table: update the `sort_order` row to document
  `"new"`, `"criticscore"`, `"userscore"`; rename the
  `min_metascore`/`min_metascore_reviews` rows to the critic names.
- Tests:
  - Config parsing accepts all three sort values and rejects unknown
    ones with a clear validation error.
  - Legacy keys (`metascore`, `min_metascore`,
    `min_metascore_reviews`) load successfully and trigger a one-time
    YAML rewrite (assert the file content afterwards, using a temp
    config file).
  - Second load after migration contains no legacy keys and does not
    rewrite again.
  - Pipeline passes `userscore` through to the else-branch flow
    (`year=0`), mirroring the existing `metascore`-mode tests.
  - Sort-change progress reset still fires on rename (string change).
  - README-accuracy tests updated for the new key names.

### 5. Error handling

- Unknown sort values fail pydantic validation with the Literal message
  listing the three options.
- The legacy mapping normalizes before validation, so no other code
  path can observe the old spellings.
- If the YAML rewrite fails (e.g. read-only filesystem), log a WARNING
  and continue with the migrated in-memory config; the rewrite retries
  next startup.

## Out of scope

- CLI flag for sort order (config-only today; unchanged).
- Early user-score filtering during browse (explicitly rejected).
- Renaming `min_user_score`/`min_user_reviews` (already
  user-appropriate names).

input.content:
# Design: date-based backlog cutoff (`max_date`) alongside the page budget

Date: 2026-11-06
Status: Approved (user reviewed design in session; spec written for implementation)

## Goal

Let the Metacritic backlog cutoff be expressed as a **date** instead of a page
count, because pages are meaningless to a human and do not correspond to games
reviewed: one page of zero-score games costs a page and yields nothing.

Constraints that shaped the design:

1. Score-ordered browsing (`sort_order: criticscore` / `userscore`) cannot use a
   date cutoff. Its browse list is score-ordered across all years, so a single
   page mixes 2015 and 2025 releases. Only `sort_order: new` browses per year,
   newest first.
2. Therefore pages cannot be removed. `max_pages` / `max_cycle_pages` remain the
   bound and pace for score modes.
3. The change is therefore **additive**: a new `max_date` key takes precedence
   over `max_pages` where dates are meaningful, and is inert where they are not.

## Decisions (user-approved)

- **Add, don't replace.** `max_date` is a new key; `max_pages` and
  `max_cycle_pages` keep working exactly as today in page mode.
- **`max_date: YYYYMM`, integer, `0` = disabled.** `0` (not `null`) is the
  disabled value, matching the project's `0 = unlimited/off` convention used by
  `max_cycle_pages` and `max_queue_days`.
- **`max_date` is a precise month floor.** In date mode the sweep walks months
  newest first, back to and including `max_date`, and inside the boundary year
  stops as soon as a page's games are all older than the floor. This reuses the
  existing `cutoff_date` early-stop in `metacritic.py`, which `pipeline.py`
  currently never passes (always `None`).
- **`max_date` is absolute.** Nothing may scan past it, whatever the pace
  setting says.
- **`max_cycle_months` is the pace in date mode.** A cycle keeps scanning until
  the release dates it has walked span `max_cycle_months`, clamped so it never
  crosses `max_date`. `0` = no month pacing (sweep to the floor, watchdog
  permitting).
- **No page guard in date mode.** A cycle is not capped by a page number; the
  `max_cycle_months` target (or the floor) is the only stop. `max_pages` and
  `max_cycle_pages` are inert in date mode.
- **No new database state.** Progress is derived from the cycle's own pages plus
  the existing per-year `backlog_progress` cursors. Nothing can go stale when
  `max_date` or `max_cycle_months` changes.
- **`cache_pages_hours` is renamed to `cache_hours` in every location** it
  exists, values unchanged, migrated in place.

## Current mechanics (verified)

- `MetacriticPlatformConfig` (`config.py:109-123`) holds `max_pages: int = 500`,
  `max_cycle_pages: int | None = 0`, `cache_pages_hours: int = 6`.
  `SourceConfigEntry` (`config.py:50-60`) holds its own
  `cache_pages_hours: int = 6` for the FitGirl/FreeGOG sitemap cache.
- `pipeline.run_acquisition` derives the year range from the page budget:
  `years_back = ceil(max_pages / 52)` (`pipeline.py:273`), then loops
  `range(current_year, cutoff_year - 1, -1)` newest-first (`pipeline.py:305`).
- A shared budget `total_scanned = db.sum_scanned_pages(...)` (`pipeline.py:281`)
  drives a "budget exhausted -> `db.reset_progress()` -> restart from page 1"
  branch (`pipeline.py:284-292`) and a percentage progress log
  (`pipeline.py:578-587`).
- Per-year resume cursors live in `backlog_progress.last_scanned_page`
  (`database.py:160-176`), read at `pipeline.py:313` and written only for pages
  really fetched (`pipeline.py:341-342`).
- A drained sweep resets progress: `_recent_games_exhausted` probes
  (`pipeline.py:348-370`).
- `MetacriticClient.scan_recent_games(..., cutoff_date=...)` already supports a
  date stop via `_should_stop_scan` / `_page_is_before_cutoff`
  (`metacritic.py:471-484`, `922-948`), but every pipeline call passes
  `cutoff_date=None` (`pipeline.py:326`).
- `scan_state.last_cutoff_date` exists (`database.py:150`) but no pipeline code
  reads or writes it; only its own DB methods and tests reference it.
- `scan_state` already has additive `ALTER TABLE` migration precedent
  (`database.py:265-270`) — not used by this design.
- Config migrations are key-presence driven and run in a fixed order
  (`config.py:912-940`), with `load_config` writing the migrated dict back and
  bumping `config_version` when any migration reports `changed=True`.
- `tests/unit/test_readme_accuracy.py` parses README config tables as exactly
  three columns and asserts README defaults against code defaults.

## Design

### 1. Mode resolution

One predicate decides everything, evaluated per cycle from the resolved
per-platform config:

```
date_mode = (max_date != 0) and (sort_order == "new")
```

| Mode | Bound | Pace | Inert (logged once per cycle) |
|------|-------|------|------------------------------|
| Date mode (`date_mode` true) | `max_date` | `max_cycle_months` | `max_pages`, `max_cycle_pages` |
| Page mode (`date_mode` false, `sort_order: new`) | `max_pages` (today) | `max_cycle_pages` (today) | `max_date`, `max_cycle_months` |
| Page mode (score modes) | `max_pages` (today) | `max_cycle_pages` (today) | `max_date`, `max_cycle_months` |

The inert-key log is emitted once per cycle at INFO, naming the keys and the
reason, e.g.:

```
Config: max_date/max_cycle_months ignored because sort_order is 'criticscore'
Config: max_pages/max_cycle_pages ignored because max_date is set (date mode)
```

### 2. Config surface (`src/gamarr/config.py`)

- `MetacriticPlatformConfig` gains:
  - `max_date: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)` — `0` disables date mode,
    otherwise `YYYYMM`.
  - `max_cycle_months: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)` — `0` = no month pacing.
  - `cache_hours: int = 6` (renamed from `cache_pages_hours`).
- `SourceConfigEntry` gains `cache_hours: int = Field(default=6, gt=0, le=168)`
  (renamed from `cache_pages_hours`).
- A `max_date` validator rejects anything that is not `0` or a six-digit
  `YYYYMM` with month `01`-`12`:

  ```
  max_date must be 0 (disabled) or YYYYMM with month 01-12, e.g. 202401
  ```

  `2024`, `202413`, `2024-01` and negative values all fail.
- A `max_date` later than the current calendar month is clamped to the current
  month with a WARNING. It is not an error: a future floor would otherwise sweep
  nothing and look like a broken install.
- Per-platform overrides inherit both keys automatically because they live on
  `MetacriticPlatformConfig`.
- The default config dict and the generated YAML show `max_date: 0` and
  `max_cycle_months: 0` with short comments, so opting in is a single edit.

### 3. Cache key rename and migration

- New migration `_migrate_cache_pages_hours_to_cache_hours(raw)` rewrites
  `cache_pages_hours` -> `cache_hours` in:
  1. every `review_sites.metacritic.platform_overrides.<platform>`,
  2. every `download_sites[].<source>` entry (FitGirl, FreeGOG, and any future
     source).
  Values are preserved, an INFO line names each migration, and it is registered
  in `_migrations` (ordered after `_migrate_download_sites_to_keyed_list` so the
  keyed-list shape already exists).
- The `config_version` bump is automatic via the existing
  `migrated=True` write-back.
- If both `cache_pages_hours` and `cache_hours` are present, `cache_hours` wins
  and the old key is removed (same rule as `_rename_config_key`).
- Historical migrations that resolve into `max_pages`
  (`_migrate_cutoff_weeks_to_max_pages`,
  `_migrate_days_since_release`, `_migrate_remove_max_games`) keep their current
  target. They describe upgrades from removed keys, not this change.

### 4. Pipeline (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py`)

`AcquisitionConfig` and `run_acquisition` gain `max_date: int = 0` and
`max_cycle_months: int = 0`; `cache_pages_hours` is renamed `cache_hours` and
`fitgirl_cache_pages_hours` is renamed `fitgirl_cache_hours`.

Date mode replaces the page-budget arithmetic for the browse phase:

```
floor_month  = clamp(max_date)                    # absolute, never crossed
year_range   = current_year down to floor_month // 100
cycle_start  = month of the first page fetched in this cycle
target_month = max(floor_month, cycle_start - max_cycle_months)
               # max_cycle_months == 0 -> target_month = floor_month

for scan_year in year_range (newest first):
    start_page = backlog_progress[scan_year].last_scanned_page + 1
    scan_recent_games(
        ...,
        year = scan_year,
        cutoff_date = "YYYY-MM-01" of target_month,   # early stop inside a year
        max_pages = 0,                                 # no page guard
    )
    advance last_scanned_page for pages really fetched   # unchanged rules

Rules:

- **`cutoff_date` is finally used.** `pipeline.py` currently passes `None`; date
  mode passes the month-start of `target_month` (which is never older than
  `floor_month`). `metacritic.py` needs no change — the stop condition already
  exists and already only applies when `sort_order == "new"`.
- **The page budget does not run in date mode.** `total_scanned`,
  `sum_scanned_pages`, the `remaining_pages` bookkeeping and the
  "budget exhausted -> reset to page 1" branch are skipped entirely. The static
  floor replaces them. Page mode keeps all of it, unchanged.
- **Month stopping uses page granularity.** A page whose games span a month
  boundary is not split; the cycle stops on the first page where every game is
  older than `target_month`. This matches the existing `max_date` floor-stop
  semantics and avoids fractional pages.
- **Page mode is untouched,** including `years_back = ceil(max_pages / 52)`.
- **Progress logging:** date mode logs
  `Backlog: reached 2025-11 (floor 2024-01, year 2025 page 12)` instead of
  `Progress: N of 500 pages scanned (x%)`. The page-mode line is unchanged.
- **Drained reset:** a cycle that reaches the floor counts as drained (the
  client's `_recent_games_exhausted` probe, clamped to the floor year) and calls
  `db.reset_progress()`, so the next sweep starts at the newest year and picks
  up new releases. This is today's drained-reset behaviour, retargeted.

  cursor untouched; a fetch failure is never read as a drain.

  for unparsable input.

# Design: date-based backlog cutoff (`max_date`) alongside the page budget

Date: 2026-11-06
Status: Approved (user reviewed design in session; spec written for implementation)

## Goal

Let the Metacritic backlog cutoff be expressed as a **date** instead of a page
count, because pages are meaningless to a human and do not correspond to games
reviewed: one page of zero-score games costs a page and yields nothing.

Constraints that shaped the design:

1. Score-ordered browsing (`sort_order: criticscore` / `userscore`) cannot use a
   date cutoff. Its browse list is score-ordered across all years, so a single
   page mixes 2015 and 2025 releases. Only `sort_order: new` browses per year,
   newest first.
2. Therefore pages cannot be removed. `max_pages` / `max_cycle_pages` remain the
   bound and pace for score modes.
3. The change is therefore **additive**: a new `max_date` key takes precedence
   over `max_pages` where dates are meaningful, and is inert where they are not.

## Decisions (user-approved)

- **Add, don't replace.** `max_date` is a new key; `max_pages` and
  `max_cycle_pages` keep working exactly as today in page mode.
- **`max_date: YYYYMM`, integer, `0` = disabled.** `0` (not `null`) is the
  disabled value, matching the project's `0 = unlimited/off` convention used by
  `max_cycle_pages` and `max_queue_days`.
- **`max_date` is a precise month floor.** In date mode the sweep walks months
  newest first, back to and including `max_date`, and inside the boundary year
  stops as soon as a page's games are all older than the floor. This reuses the
  existing `cutoff_date` early-stop in `metacritic.py`, which `pipeline.py`
  currently never passes (always `None`).
- **`max_date` is absolute.** Nothing may scan past it, whatever the pace
  setting says.
- **`max_cycle_months` is the pace in date mode.** A cycle keeps scanning until
  the release dates it has walked span `max_cycle_months`, clamped so it never
  crosses `max_date`. `0` = no month pacing (sweep to the floor, watchdog
  permitting).
- **No page guard in date mode.** A cycle is not capped by a page number; the
  `max_cycle_months` target (or the floor) is the only stop. `max_pages` and
  `max_cycle_pages` are inert in date mode.
- **No new database state.** Progress is derived from the cycle's own pages plus
  the existing per-year `backlog_progress` cursors. Nothing can go stale when
  `max_date` or `max_cycle_months` changes.
- **`cache_pages_hours` is renamed to `cache_hours` in every location** it
  exists, values unchanged, migrated in place.

## Current mechanics (verified)

- `MetacriticPlatformConfig` (`config.py:109-123`) holds `max_pages: int = 500`,
  `max_cycle_pages: int | None = 0`, `cache_pages_hours: int = 6`.
  `SourceConfigEntry` (`config.py:50-60`) holds its own
  `cache_pages_hours: int = 6` for the FitGirl/FreeGOG sitemap cache.
- `pipeline.run_acquisition` derives the year range from the page budget:
  `years_back = ceil(max_pages / 52)` (`pipeline.py:273`), then loops
  `range(current_year, cutoff_year - 1, -1)` newest-first (`pipeline.py:305`).
- A shared budget `total_scanned = db.sum_scanned_pages(...)` (`pipeline.py:281`)
  drives a "budget exhausted -> `db.reset_progress()` -> restart from page 1"
  branch (`pipeline.py:284-292`) and a percentage progress log
  (`pipeline.py:578-587`).
- Per-year resume cursors live in `backlog_progress.last_scanned_page`
  (`database.py:160-176`), read at `pipeline.py:313` and written only for pages
  really fetched (`pipeline.py:341-342`).
- A drained sweep resets progress: `_recent_games_exhausted` probes
  (`pipeline.py:348-370`).
- `MetacriticClient.scan_recent_games(..., cutoff_date=...)` already supports a
  date stop via `_should_stop_scan` / `_page_is_before_cutoff`
  (`metacritic.py:471-484`, `922-948`), but every pipeline call passes
  `cutoff_date=None` (`pipeline.py:326`).
- `scan_state.last_cutoff_date` exists (`database.py:150`) but no pipeline code
  reads or writes it; only its own DB methods and tests reference it.
- `scan_state` already has additive `ALTER TABLE` migration precedent
  (`database.py:265-270`) — not used by this design.
- Config migrations are key-presence driven and run in a fixed order
  (`config.py:912-940`), with `load_config` writing the migrated dict back and
  bumping `config_version` when any migration reports `changed=True`.
- `tests/unit/test_readme_accuracy.py` parses README config tables as exactly
  three columns and asserts README defaults against code defaults.

```text

| Mode | Bound | Pace | Inert |

| Date mode (`date_mode` true) | `max_date` | `max_cycle_months` | `max_pages`, `max_cycle_pages` |
| Page mode (`sort_order: new`, `max_date` 0) | `max_pages` (today) | `max_cycle_pages` (today) | none - date keys unset |

### 4. Pipeline (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py`)

`AcquisitionConfig` and `run_acquisition` gain `max_date: int = 0` and
`max_cycle_months: int = 0`; `cache_pages_hours` is renamed `cache_hours` and
`fitgirl_cache_pages_hours` is renamed `fitgirl_cache_hours`.

Date mode replaces the page-budget arithmetic for the browse phase:

```text
floor_month  = clamp(max_date)                    # absolute, never crossed
year_range   = current_year down to floor_month // 100
cycle_start  = month of the first page fetched in this cycle
target_month = max(floor_month, cycle_start - max_cycle_months)
               # max_cycle_months == 0 -> target_month = floor_month

for scan_year in year_range (newest first):
    start_page = backlog_progress[scan_year].last_scanned_page + 1
    scan_recent_games(
        ...,
        year = scan_year,
        cutoff_date = "YYYY-MM-01" of target_month,   # early stop inside a year
        max_pages = 0,                                 # no page guard
    )
    advance last_scanned_page for pages really fetched   # unchanged rules
    stop this cycle when a page's games are all older than target_month
```

Rules:

- **`cutoff_date` is finally used.** `pipeline.py` currently passes `None`; date
  mode passes the month-start of `target_month` (which is never older than
  `floor_month`). The stop condition itself already exists and already only
  applies when `sort_order == "new"`.
- **The page budget does not run in date mode.** `total_scanned`,
  `sum_scanned_pages`, the `remaining_pages` bookkeeping and the
  "budget exhausted -> reset to page 1" branch are skipped entirely. The static
  floor replaces them. Page mode keeps all of it, unchanged.
- **Month stopping uses page granularity.** A page whose games span a month
  boundary is not split; the cycle stops on the first page where every game is
  older than `target_month`. This matches the existing `max_date` floor-stop
  semantics and avoids fractional pages.
- **Page mode is untouched,** including `years_back = ceil(max_pages / 52)`.
- **Progress logging:** date mode logs
  `Backlog: reached 2025-11 (floor 2024-01, year 2025 page 12)` instead of
  `Progress: N of 500 pages scanned (x%)`. The page-mode line is unchanged.
- **A cutoff stop needs its own signal.** `_should_stop_scan` returns a bare
  bool, so the pipeline cannot tell "stopped because the cutoff page was
  reached" from "stopped because pages ran out". Without that distinction the
  floor year would re-fetch the same page forever: a cutoff stop collects no
  games and reports zero pages fetched, so neither `_recent_games_exhausted`
  nor `_recent_games_failed` fires and no reset ever happens.
  `MetacriticClient` therefore gains one additive flag,
  `_recent_games_cutoff_reached`, set beside the existing
  `_recent_games_exhausted` / `_recent_games_failed` flags.
- **Drained reset:** the sweep is complete when the floor year finishes, either
  by listing exhaustion or by the cutoff stop (the cutoff only counts when
  `target_month` is clamped to the floor, so a *pacing* cutoff never ends a
  sweep), and no fetch failed. That calls `db.reset_progress()`, so the next
  sweep starts at the newest year and picks up new releases. This is today's
  drained-reset behaviour, retargeted.
- **Unparsable release dates:** if the pages collected so far this cycle yield
  no parsable `release_date`, month pacing cannot be evaluated, so the cycle
  runs to the floor or the end of the listing rather than stopping on absent
  evidence.
- The year loop's per-year `except` still marks `fetch_failed` and leaves the
  cursor untouched; a fetch failure is never read as a drain.

## Error handling

| Condition | Behaviour |
| ----------- | ----------- |
| `max_date` not `0` and not `YYYYMM` | Config error at load with the message above |
| `max_date` later than the current month | WARNING, clamped to the current month |
| `max_date` set, `sort_order` is a score mode | Date keys inert, one INFO line per cycle |
| `max_date` set, `max_pages` also set | `max_pages` inert in date mode, one INFO line per cycle |
| `max_cycle_months` 0 | No month pacing; sweep to the floor |
| `max_cycle_months` larger than the span to the floor | Stops at the floor |
| Cycle hits `acquisition_timeout_mins` | Watchdog aborts; cursors only advanced for pages really fetched, so the next cycle resumes without redoing work. Raising `acquisition_timeout_mins` is the documented remedy |
| Fetch failure in a year | `fetch_failed` set, cursor untouched, not counted as drained |
| Cancellation mid-cycle | Partial results returned, fetched-page cursors kept |
| YAML rewrite fails (read-only config) | WARNING, continue with migrated in-memory config; retried next start |

    """Try to parse an ISO (``YYYY-MM-DD``) or UK (``DD-MM-YYYY``) date string."""
    for fmt in ("%Y-%m-%d", "%d-%m-%Y"):

def _find_config_block(lines: list[str], heading: str) -> list[str] | None:
    """Find a config table block under *heading* in the README lines.

    Returns the table rows following *heading*, or None if *heading* is
    not found. The block ends at the first non-table line.
    """
    start = None
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip().startswith(f"### `{heading}`") or line.strip().startswith(f"#### `{heading}`"):
            start = i
            break
    if start is None:

    # Skip the heading and the table header row
    block: list[str] = []

        elif in_table:

    return block

`metacritic.py` the cutoff logic already exists; the additions are the
`_recent_games_cutoff_reached` flag and the `max_month_span` parameter described
under Refinements below.

## Refinements found while planning

1. **The month pace needs a client-side span parameter.** The cycle's month
   target is derived from the month of the first page the cycle fetches, and
   only `MetacriticClient` sees per-page release dates before deciding whether to
   stop. Passing a precomputed `cutoff_date` for the pace is therefore
   impossible on the first call of a cycle (the origin is unknown), and handling
   it in the pipeline would leave the first call of every cycle unbounded within
   its year. `scan_recent_games` therefore gains `max_month_span: int = 0`; the
   client anchors the span on the newest month of the call's first page and stops
   when a page's games are all older than `origin - max_month_span`. The pipeline
   still shares the allowance across years exactly as it shares
   `max_cycle_pages` today: it passes the *remaining* span to each subsequent
   year and stops visiting older years once the allowance is spent, so a cycle
   cannot take a full allowance from every year.
2. **One flag still suffices.** The client folds the pace boundary and the
   absolute floor into a single effective cutoff, so a single
   `_recent_games_cutoff_reached` flag reports "stopped on a date boundary". The
   pipeline distinguishes a floor stop from a pace stop by comparing its own
   months-covered against the span to the floor, as specified.

# Date-based backlog cutoff (`max_date`) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use sub-agents (recommended) to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add a human-readable `max_date: YYYYMM` backlog cutoff plus a `max_cycle_months` pace for `sort_order: new`, and rename the config key `cache_pages_hours` to `cache_hours`, without changing page-mode behaviour.

**Architecture:** `max_date` is a month floor enforced by the browse scan's existing (but never used) `cutoff_date` early-stop; `max_cycle_months` is enforced client-side as a month span anchored on each call's first page, with the pipeline sharing the allowance across years exactly as it shares `max_cycle_pages` today. Page mode (`max_pages` + `max_cycle_pages`) is untouched, and no database schema or persisted frontier state is added. The cache rename rides the existing key-presence migration mechanism.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, pydantic v2, pytest, ruff, mypy, `uv`, loguru.

**Spec:** `docs/agent/specs/2026-11-06-max-date-backlog-cutoff-design.md` (approved, includes the two planning refinements below).

def subtract_months(year_month: int, months: int) -> int:
    """Return *year_month* (``YYYYMM``) reduced by *months* months.

    ``months <= 0`` returns *year_month* unchanged, matching the project's
    ``0 = no limit`` convention.

    Args:
        year_month: A ``YYYYMM`` value, e.g. ``202511``.
        months: Whole months to subtract.

    Returns:
        The resulting ``YYYYMM`` value.
    """
    if months <= 0:
        return year_month
    index = (year_month // 100) * 12 + (year_month % 100 - 1) - months
    return (index // 12) * 100 + (index % 12) + 1


def month_of(date_str: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Return the ``YYYYMM`` month of a release-date string.

    Accepts the ISO (``YYYY-MM-DD``) and UK (``DD-MM-YYYY``) shapes the
    Metacritic scrubbing already tolerates.

    Args:
        date_str: The date string, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The ``YYYYMM`` month, or ``None`` when absent or unparsable.
    """
    if not date_str:
        return None
    for fmt in ("%Y-%m-%d", "%d-%m-%Y"):
        try:
            parsed = datetime.datetime.strptime(date_str.strip(), fmt)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            continue
        return parsed.year * 100 + parsed.month
    return None


def year_month_to_date(year_month: int) -> str:
    """Return the first day of a ``YYYYMM`` month as an ISO date string.

    Args:
        year_month: A ``YYYYMM`` value, e.g. ``202401``.

    Returns:
        ``"YYYY-MM-01"``, the form the browse scan's ``cutoff_date`` expects.
    """
    return f"{year_month // 100:04d}-{year_month % 100:02d}-01"
```

    @field_validator("max_date")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_max_date(cls, value: int) -> int:
        """Validate ``YYYYMM`` and clamp a future floor to the current month.

        ``0`` disables date mode. A floor later than the current calendar
        month would sweep nothing, so it is clamped rather than rejected.

        Args:
            value: The configured ``max_date``.

        Returns:
            The validated (possibly clamped) month.

        Raises:
            ValueError: When *value* is neither 0 nor a valid ``YYYYMM`` month.
        """
        if value == 0:
            return 0
        if value < 0 or not 100001 <= value <= 999912 or not 1 <= value % 100 <= 12:
            raise ValueError("max_date must be 0 (disabled) or YYYYMM with month 01-12, e.g. 202401")
        now = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC)
        current_month = now.year * 100 + now.month
        if value > current_month:
            logger.warning(
                "Config: max_date {} is in the future — clamping to {}",
                value,
                current_month,
            )
            return current_month
        return value

def _migrate_cache_pages_hours_to_cache_hours(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Rename ``cache_pages_hours`` to ``cache_hours`` for every owner.

    The key exists on two different models — the Metacritic platform config
    (browse-page cache) and each download source (sitemap cache) — so both
    shapes are migrated here. Values are preserved.

    Args:
        raw: The raw YAML config dict, mutated in place.

    Returns:
        True when at least one key was renamed or cleaned up.
    """
    changed = False

    mc_cfg = raw.get("review_sites")
    if isinstance(mc_cfg, dict):
        metacritic = mc_cfg.get("metacritic")
        if isinstance(metacritic, dict):
            overrides = metacritic.get("platform_overrides")
            if isinstance(overrides, dict):
                for platform_key, platform_cfg in overrides.items():
                    if isinstance(platform_cfg, dict):
                        changed |= _rename_config_key(
                            platform_cfg,
                            "cache_pages_hours",
                            "cache_hours",
                            str(platform_key),
                        )

    download_sites = raw.get("download_sites")
    if isinstance(download_sites, list):
        for entry in download_sites:
            if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry:
                source_name = str(list(entry.keys())[0])
                body = entry[list(entry.keys())[0]]
                if isinstance(body, dict):
                    changed |= _rename_config_key(body, "cache_pages_hours", "cache_hours", source_name)

    return changed

```python
def _month_span(newer: int | None, older: int | None) -> int:
    """Return whole months between two ``YYYYMM`` values.

    Args:
        newer: The newer ``YYYYMM`` month, or ``None``.
        older: The older ``YYYYMM`` month, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        Whole months from *older* to *newer*; 0 when either side is unknown.
    """
    if not newer or not older:
        return 0
    return max(0, (newer // 100) * 12 + newer % 100 - ((older // 100) * 12 + older % 100))
```

def subtract_months(year_month: int, months: int) -> int:
    """Return *year_month* (``YYYYMM``) reduced by *months* months.

    ``months <= 0`` returns *year_month* unchanged, matching the project's
    ``0 = no limit`` convention.

    Args:
        year_month: A ``YYYYMM`` value, e.g. ``202511``.
        months: Whole months to subtract.

    Returns:
        The resulting ``YYYYMM`` value.
    """
    if months <= 0:
        return year_month
    index = (year_month // 100) * 12 + (year_month % 100 - 1) - months
    return (index // 12) * 100 + (index % 12) + 1


def month_of(date_str: str | None) -> int | None:
    """Return the ``YYYYMM`` month of a release-date string.

    Accepts the ISO (``YYYY-MM-DD``) and UK (``DD-MM-YYYY``) shapes the
    Metacritic scrubbing already tolerates.

    Args:
        date_str: The date string, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The ``YYYYMM`` month, or ``None`` when absent or unparsable.
    """
    if not date_str:
        return None
    for fmt in ("%Y-%m-%d", "%d-%m-%Y"):
        try:
            parsed = datetime.datetime.strptime(date_str.strip(), fmt)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            continue
        return parsed.year * 100 + parsed.month
    return None


def year_month_to_date(year_month: int) -> str:
    """Return the first day of a ``YYYYMM`` month as an ISO date string.

    Args:
        year_month: A ``YYYYMM`` value, e.g. ``202401``.

    Returns:
        ``"YYYY-MM-01"``, the form the browse scan's ``cutoff_date`` expects.
    """
    return f"{year_month // 100:04d}-{year_month % 100:02d}-01"

    @field_validator("max_date")
    @classmethod
    def _validate_max_date(cls, value: int) -> int:
        """Validate ``YYYYMM`` and clamp a future floor to the current month.

        ``0`` disables date mode. A floor later than the current calendar
        month would sweep nothing, so it is clamped rather than rejected.

        Args:
            value: The configured ``max_date``.

        Returns:
            The validated (possibly clamped) month.

        Raises:
            ValueError: When *value* is neither 0 nor a valid ``YYYYMM`` month.
        """
        if value == 0:
            return 0
        if value < 0 or not 100001 <= value <= 999912 or not 1 <= value % 100 <= 12:
            raise ValueError("max_date must be 0 (disabled) or YYYYMM with month 01-12, e.g. 202401")
        now = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC)
        current_month = now.year * 100 + now.month
        if value > current_month:
            logger.warning(
                "Config: max_date {} is in the future — clamping to {}",
                value,
                current_month,
            )
            return current_month
        return value

for path, names in removals.items():
    p = pathlib.Path(path)
    src = p.read_text()
    lines = src.split("\n")
    spans = []
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in names:
            # extend upward over decorators, downward over trailing blank line
            start = node.lineno - 1
            for dec in getattr(node, "decorator_list", []):
                start = min(start, dec.lineno - 1)
            end = node.end_lineno - 1
            spans.append((start, end))
    spans.sort(reverse=True)
    for start, end in spans:
        while end + 1 < len(lines) and lines[end + 1].strip() == "":
            end += 1
        del lines[start:end + 1]
    p.write_text("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"{path}: removed {len(spans)} test(s) -> {names}")

        self,
        platform: str,
        *,
        max_games: int = 0,
        max_pages: int = 0,
        max_month_span: int = 0,
        cache_pages_hours: int = 6,

        cancel_event: threading.Event | None = None,
        start_page: int = 1,
        show_progress: bool = False,
    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Collect games from Metacritic browse pages.

        Fetches browse pages (newest-first) and collects games until
        *max_games* is reached, pages run out, or *cutoff_date*
        causes an early stop (when every game on a page is older than
        the cutoff).  With default max_games=0 (unlimited), the
        cutoff_date is the primary limiter.

        Args:
            max_games: Maximum number of game entries to collect (0 = unlimited).
            max_month_span: Stop once a page's games are all older than
                ``first page month - max_month_span`` (0 = no month pacing).
                The span is anchored on the newest release date of this
                call's first page, so a caller that wants a budget shared
                across calls must pass the remaining allowance each time.
            cutoff_date: Date string in "YYYY-MM-DD" or "DD-MM-YYYY" format.
                Pages whose games are all older than this date are skipped.
            cancel_event: Optional threading.Event.  When set, the
                scan stops early and returns partial results.
            start_page: Page number to start scanning from.  Pages 1..start_page-1
                are skipped without fetching.  This avoids re-traversing
                already-known pages when the backlog resumes after a
                config change.
            show_progress: When True, log page-level progress heartbeats
                during long cold-cache scans.

        Returns a list of game dicts with keys ``title``, ``slug``,
        ``score``, ``critic_review_count``, ``user_rating``,
        ``user_review_count``, ``release_date``.
        """
        all_games: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

        cutoff_date = _validate_cutoff_date(cutoff_date)

        effective_max = max_games if max_games > 0 else 999999
        start_page = max(1, start_page)
        page_number = start_page
        self._recent_games_exhausted = False
        self._recent_games_failed = False
        self._recent_games_cutoff_reached = False
        span_anchor: int | None = None
        while len(all_games) < effective_max and page_number <= 2000:
            games = self._fetch_browse_page(platform, page_number, cache_pages_hours, year=year)
            if games is None:
                # Fetch or parse failure — this year is not drained, so the
                # caller must keep its progress row untouched.
                self._recent_games_failed = True
                break

def _rename_metacritic_cache_hours(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Rename ``cache_pages_hours`` on every Metacritic platform override.

    Args:
        raw: The raw YAML config dict, mutated in place.

    Returns:
        True when at least one override key was renamed or cleaned up.
    """
    review_sites = raw.get("review_sites")
    if not isinstance(review_sites, dict):
        return False
    metacritic = review_sites.get("metacritic")
    if not isinstance(metacritic, dict):
        return False
    overrides = metacritic.get("platform_overrides")
    if not isinstance(overrides, dict):
        return False
    changed = False
    for platform_key, platform_cfg in overrides.items():
        if isinstance(platform_cfg, dict):
            changed |= _rename_config_key(platform_cfg, "cache_pages_hours", "cache_hours", str(platform_key))
    return changed


def _rename_source_cache_hours(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Rename ``cache_pages_hours`` on every download-source entry.

    Args:
        raw: The raw YAML config dict, mutated in place.

    Returns:
        True when at least one source key was renamed or cleaned up.
    """
    download_sites = raw.get("download_sites")
    if not isinstance(download_sites, list):
        return False
    changed = False
    for entry in download_sites:
        if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry:
            source_name = str(list(entry.keys())[0])
            body = entry[list(entry.keys())[0]]
            if isinstance(body, dict):
                changed |= _rename_config_key(body, "cache_pages_hours", "cache_hours", source_name)
    return changed


def _migrate_cache_pages_hours_to_cache_hours(raw: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Rename ``cache_pages_hours`` to ``cache_hours`` for every owner.

    The key exists on two different models — the Metacritic platform config
    (browse-page cache) and each download source (sitemap cache) — so both
    shapes are migrated here. Values are preserved.

    Args:
        raw: The raw YAML config dict, mutated in place.

    Returns:
        True when at least one key was renamed or cleaned up.
    """
    changed = _rename_metacritic_cache_hours(raw)
    changed |= _rename_source_cache_hours(raw)
    return changed

class TestBrowseScanHelpers:
    """Unit tests for the pure helpers extracted from scan_recent_games."""

    def test_effective_page_cap_treats_zero_and_negative_as_unlimited(self) -> None:
        from gamarr.metacritic import _effective_page_cap

        assert _effective_page_cap(0) == 999999
        assert _effective_page_cap(-4) == 999999
        assert _effective_page_cap(7) == 7

    def test_page_newest_month_empty_page(self) -> None:
        from gamarr.metacritic import _page_newest_month

        assert _page_newest_month([]) is None
        assert _page_newest_month([{"title": "A"}]) is None

    def test_page_newest_month_ignores_unparsable_dates(self) -> None:
        from gamarr.metacritic import _page_newest_month

        page = [
            {"release_date": "2025-03-04"},
            {"release_date": None},
            {"release_date": "garbage"},
            {"release_date": "04-11-2025"},
        ]
        assert _page_newest_month(page) == 202511

    def test_effective_cutoff_without_span_returns_absolute_cutoff(self) -> None:
        from gamarr.metacritic import _effective_cutoff

        assert _effective_cutoff("2024-01-01", 202511, 0) == "2024-01-01"
        assert _effective_cutoff("2024-01-01", None, 2) == "2024-01-01"
        assert _effective_cutoff(None, None, 0) is None

    def test_effective_cutoff_span_wins_when_newer(self) -> None:
        from gamarr.metacritic import _effective_cutoff

        assert _effective_cutoff("2024-01-01", 202511, 2) == "2025-09-01"

    def test_effective_cutoff_absolute_wins_when_newer(self) -> None:
        from gamarr.metacritic import _effective_cutoff

        assert _effective_cutoff("2025-10-01", 202511, 2) == "2025-10-01"

    def test_page_stop_decision_flags_a_cutoff_page(self) -> None:
        from gamarr.metacritic import _page_stop_decision

        page = [{"release_date": "2019-05-01"}]
        stop, cutoff_reached = _page_stop_decision("new", page, "2024-01-01", 0, None, 0, 1, 1)
        assert stop is True
        assert cutoff_reached is True

    def test_page_stop_decision_collects_a_recent_page(self) -> None:
        from gamarr.metacritic import _page_stop_decision

        page = [{"release_date": "2025-11-01"}]
        stop, cutoff_reached = _page_stop_decision("new", page, "2024-01-01", 0, None, 0, 1, 1)
        assert stop is False
        assert cutoff_reached is False

    def test_classify_page_marks_cancellation_without_touching_drain_flags(self) -> None:
        import threading

        client = MetacriticClient.__new__(MetacriticClient)
        client._recent_games_exhausted = False
        client._recent_games_failed = False
        cancel_event = threading.Event()
        cancel_event.set()

        stopped = client._classify_page([{"release_date": "2025-11-01"}], 1, 3, cancel_event)

        assert stopped is True
        assert client._recent_games_exhausted is False
        assert client._recent_games_failed is False

    def test_classify_page_failure_and_exhaustion(self) -> None:
        client = MetacriticClient.__new__(MetacriticClient)
        client._recent_games_exhausted = False
        client._recent_games_failed = False

        assert client._classify_page(None, 1, 1, None) is True
        assert client._recent_games_failed is True

        assert client._classify_page([], 2, 2, None) is True
        assert client._recent_games_exhausted is True

result.output:
## Review

**Review basis / limitation:** shell git is unavailable to me in this session, so I could not run `git diff origin/main`. I reviewed the complete working‑tree delta against launch HEAD (`watchdog_diff` for `src/`, `tests/`, `README.md` — 16 files, 1141 insertions) and read the named files in full (`config.py`, `metacritic.py`, `pipeline.py`, `scheduler.py`, `utils.py`, plus `database.py`, `library.py`, `pyproject.toml` and the changed test files). The delta contains exactly the described feature, so I treat it as the change under review; any hunk that exists only in a commit between `origin/main` and HEAD would not have been visible.

### Correct (verified, not assumed)
- **`max_date == 0` leaves page mode identical.** Hunk-by-hunk: `total_scanned`/budget reset/`remaining_pages`/`cycle_allowance` moved into the `else` branch unchanged (`pipeline.py:322-341`), the year‑loop guards are byte-identical for page mode (`pipeline.py:363-372`), `cutoff_date=None`/`max_month_span=0` are no‑ops in the client (`_effective_cutoff` returns `cutoff_date`; `_page_is_before_cutoff(None)` is `False`, so `_recent_games_cutoff_reached` never latches), and the drained‑reset block is unchanged (`pipeline.py:468-479`). The only page-mode deviation is finding 1.
- **Month arithmetic is right.** `subtract_months` uses a zero-based index correctly: `202501-1 → 202412`, `202601-2 → 202511`, `202401-1 → 202312`; `_month_span` cancels the 1‑based offset and clamps at 0; `year_month_to_date` yields the ISO first-of-month the cutoff parser expects.
- **Floor beats pace.** `_effective_cutoff` takes the newer of the two cutoffs (`metacritic.py:995-998`), and the pace is re-clamped by the floor in every call, matching the spec's "max_date is absolute" rule.
- **Migration ordering is right.** `_migrate_cache_pages_hours_to_cache_hours` (`config.py:1048`) runs after the legacy `cache_ttl_hours → cache_pages_hours` renames (`config.py:307-323`, `558-580`) and before the freegog default injection — including in the flat-dict and flat-list legacy shapes, because the shape migrations run earlier (`config.py:1029-1039`). `_deep_merge` passes raw list entries through, so an injected default cannot overwrite a migrated source value; `cache_hours` wins only when the user really set both.
- **MagicMock truthiness trap is defused in the production code.** Every flag read is `getattr(...) is True` (`pipeline.py:418-419, 436, 513`), so a MagicMock attribute cannot fake "drained"/"failed". The new tests also set all four flags explicitly.
- The metacritic extraction (`_classify_page`, `_page_stop_decision`, `_effective_page_cap`, `_page_newest_month`) is behaviour-preserving for the pre-existing paths: stop-before-trim ordering, cancel-ordering, `last_page`/`pages_fetched` computation and progress logging are unchanged.

### Findings

**1. HIGH — the pipeline calls `scan_recent_games` with a keyword the client does not accept, and the resulting `TypeError` is swallowed: no browsing ever happens in page mode or date mode.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:396` (`cache_hours=cfg.cache_hours`) vs `src/gamarr/metacritic.py:859-866` (`cache_pages_hours: int = 6`, used positionally at `metacritic.py:918`).
What is wrong: the rename was applied to the client call site, but the client signature deliberately kept `cache_pages_hours` (the plan states this explicitly). Every `mc.scan_recent_games(...)` call therefore raises `TypeError: scan_recent_games() got an unexpected keyword argument 'cache_hours'`.
Why it matters: the call sits inside `try:` at `pipeline.py:381-447`, so the exception is caught by the broad `except Exception` (`pipeline.py:443-445`), logged as "Scan failed for year …", and the loop simply moves to the next year. Result: zero browse games on every cycle, `0 games browsed`, and — because `fetch_failed` is now always true with an empty `browse_games` — a scrape-failure notification each cycle. It is a silent total loss of discovery (the daemon keeps "succeeding"), and it breaks page mode too, not just the new date mode. No test catches it because every pipeline test substitutes a MagicMock for `MetacriticClient`/`scan_recent_games` (`tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:8655, 697, 726, …`), and no test asserts the forwarded kwargs of the real method.
Smallest fix: pass `cache_pages_hours=cfg.cache_hours` at `pipeline.py:396` (or add a `cache_hours` alias to the client) and add one test that asserts the forwarded kwarg against the real `MetacriticClient.scan_recent_games` signature (e.g. `inspect.signature`), not a MagicMock.

**2. HIGH — `range_empty` is computed from a page counter that excludes the call that ended on a cutoff, so a paced date sweep resets all progress mid-sweep and never advances past its first pace window.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:436-440` and `src/gamarr/pipeline.py:457`.
What is wrong: when `_recent_games_cutoff_reached` is true the loop does `cutoff_stopped = True; break` **before** `pages_this_cycle += pages_scanned` (`:440`). The final call's pages are therefore never counted. In a paced sweep (`max_cycle_months > 0`) the steady state is: newest year already exhausted → its probe yields 0 pages but `drained_probes = 1`; the next year's first call walks its pace window and stops on the span cutoff → `pages_this_cycle` stays `0`. Then `range_empty = pages_this_cycle == 0 and drained_probes > 0` is `True`, `sweep_complete` becomes `True` (the comment says this branch means "every year in the range probed empty"), and `db.reset_progress(platform, …)` (`:461-466`) wipes **all** per-year cursors — `reset_progress` deletes every row for the platform (`src/gamarr/database.py:531-539`).
Why it matters: with pacing the older year's cursor is erased before it can accumulate, so the sweep oscillates: re-sweep the newest year in full, take one pace window of the next year, reset again. The documented promise ("`max_cycle_months` limits how many months of backlog a single cycle covers", README:184) is not achieved — the sweep never reaches the floor and re-fetches the newest year indefinitely. It also makes the per-cycle log line (`:688-693`) under-report pages by the last segment.
Smallest fix: count the pages of the cutoff-stopped call as well (move `pages_this_cycle += pages_scanned` above the `if date_mode:` block, or add a separate `scanned_any_page` flag set from `pages_scanned`), then gate `range_empty` on that. `src/gamarr/pipeline.py` (plus a test in `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`: drained year followed by a span-cutoff year must **not** reset progress).

**3. MEDIUM — `_effective_cutoff` compares cutoffs as strings, but `cutoff_date` is documented to also accept `DD-MM-YYYY`; mixing formats silently picks the wrong bound.**
`src/gamarr/metacritic.py:995-998`, with `_validate_cutoff_date` at `metacritic.py:530-539` returning the caller's string unchanged.
What is wrong: `span_cutoff > cutoff_date` is a lexical compare between an ISO string produced by `year_month_to_date` and whatever the caller supplied. `scan_recent_games("pc", cutoff_date="01-03-2024", max_month_span=2)` compares `"2025-01-01" > "01-03-2024"` → `True`, so the pace cutoff replaces a floor that is actually *newer* — the scan walks past the absolute floor, contradicting "`max_date` is absolute, nothing may scan past it". A leading/trailing space in the cutoff has the same effect (`_parse_date_flexible` strips, `>` does not).
Why it matters: latent contract break in a new helper — the pipeline only sends ISO today, but `scan_recent_games` is a public method whose docstring advertises both formats, and the failure mode is "quietly ignores/overrides the floor".
Smallest fix: normalise both sides to `datetime.date` before comparing (reuse `_parse_date_flexible`) and compare dates, not strings, in `src/gamarr/metacritic.py`.

**4. LOW — `covered >= span_to_floor` is one month too strict when pacing is enabled, so a cycle that actually reached the floor does not do the completion reset.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:456` with `_month_span` at `:111-126`.
What is wrong: `covered = max_month_seen - min_month_seen` and `span_to_floor = max_month_seen - floor_month` (difference convention). If the floor month itself has no releases, the last accepted page's newest month is `floor+1`, so `covered == span_to_floor - 1` and `at_floor` is `False` even though the following page was a genuine floor stop. (The unpaced case is unaffected because `not cfg.max_cycle_months` short-circuits the whole guard.)
Why it matters: only an extra empty probe cycle before the reset, and a missing "Backlog complete" log; the sweep still converges, so this is polish rather than a defect in outcome.
Smallest fix: compare the months directly — `min_month_seen is not None and min_month_seen <= floor_month` — in `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`.

**5. LOW — the pace overshoots by about one month whenever a cycle crosses a year boundary, because each client call re-anchors on its own first page while the pipeline only subtracts the months it has already counted.**
`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:378-383` (`month_span_left = max_cycle_months - _month_span(max_month_seen, min_month_seen)`) with `src/gamarr/metacritic.py:919-922` (`span_anchor` per call).
What is wrong: after year *Y*'s listing is exhausted, the remaining allowance is passed to year *Y−1*, whose anchor is ~one month older than the last month walked. The resulting cutoff is `origin − budget − 1`, i.e. the cycle collects one extra month of backlog. The spec's intended `target_month = max(floor, cycle_start − max_cycle_months)` is therefore approximate, not exact.
Why it matters: `max_cycle_months` is a speed knob, so a one-month overshoot is cosmetic, but it makes the documented pace slightly wrong at every year boundary.
Smallest fix: keep one cycle-level anchor (pass the cycle's anchor month, or a precomputed cutoff) instead of re-deriving per call, in `src/gamarr/pipeline.py` / `src/gamarr/metacritic.py`.

**6. LOW — `max_date` has no lower sanity bound, so a typo like `100001` produces a ~1000-year year loop.**
`src/gamarr/config.py:149` (`100001 <= value <= 999912`).
What is wrong: any 6-digit value with month 01‑12 passes; `cutoff_year = floor_month // 100` then makes `range(current_year, cutoff_year-1, -1)` iterate ~1000 times, each iteration issuing a browse fetch for a year with no data (and an empty-listing probe every cycle thereafter).
Why it matters: an unrealistic but accepted config turns one cycle into ~1000 HTTP requests; cheap to reject.
Smallest fix: add a floor (e.g. `>= 200001`) to the validator in `src/gamarr/config.py`, with the matching test in `tests/unit/test_config.py`.

**7. LOW — README phase 2 still states that `max_cycle_pages` caps the per-cycle page limit, contradicting phase 1's "unused in date mode".**
`README.md:317-322` versus `README.md:310-316` and `max_cycle_pages` being inert at `pipeline.py:364-371`.
Why it matters: incorrect docs for changed behaviour in exactly the section a date-mode user will read.
Smallest fix: qualify phase 2 ("in page mode; date mode is bounded by `max_date`/`max_cycle_months`") in `README.md`.

**8. LOW — the documented migration-ordering invariant has no regression test.**
`src/gamarr/config.py:1043-1048`; tests at `tests/unit/test_config.py:1821-1885`.
What is wrong: the comment says the rename must precede the freegog default injection or "its value would be discarded in favour of the default", but no test covers a sparse freegog entry that only has the legacy key (`{"freegog": {"cache_pages_hours": 9}}` must end as `cache_hours: 9`, not `6`). I traced the current order and it is correct — only the guard is missing, and swapping the two entries would silently break it again.
Smallest fix: add that one case to `tests/unit/test_config.py`.

**9. LOW — unrelated deletions in the same delta remove coverage of existing, still-present APIs.**
`tests/unit/test_database.py` (`test_reset_progress_new_sort`, `test_update_pending_scores_nonexistent`) and `tests/unit/test_library.py` (`test_check_game_not_found_no_index`).
What is wrong: `Database.update_pending_scores` (`database.py:592`) and `LibraryScanner.check_game` (`library.py:189`) still exist, and `reset_progress` deleting multiple year rows is now relied on more heavily by date mode. If these deletions belong to a different change, they should not be in this one; if they are deliberate, they need a reason.
Why it matters: silent coverage loss in the same commit — and the `reset_progress` case is precisely the invariant the new date-mode reset depends on.
Smallest fix: restore the three tests (or split them into their own commit) in `tests/unit/test_database.py` / `tests/unit/test_library.py`.

No HIGH findings other than 1 and 2, and **no security or concurrency findings at all** (no new I/O surface, the new flags are per-instance and `scan_recent_games` is not called concurrently).

### Tests the supervisor must run
`uv run pytest tests/unit/test_pipeline.py tests/unit/test_metacritic.py tests/unit/test_config.py tests/unit/test_scheduler.py tests/unit/test_utils.py tests/unit/test_readme_accuracy.py -q`, then the full `uv run pytest --cov=gamarr --cov-fail-under=80`, plus `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run mypy .`. Note that the whole suite can pass with finding 1 present, because `MetacriticClient` is mocked everywhere.

**Merge verdict: BLOCK** (findings 1 and 2 are live functional breaks in the feature and in the untouched page‑mode path).
