## Review

Scope: I inspected the working-tree delta (src/, tests/, README.md) and read the complete current `config.py`, `metacritic.py`, `pipeline.py`, `scheduler.py`, `utils.py` plus the changed test files. I did not modify any file. I could not run git/tests (no shell tool), so the command to run is listed at the end.

**Correct (round-1 fixes verified)**

- Pipeline→client kwarg is fixed: `pipeline.py:405` sends `cache_pages_hours=cfg.cache_hours`, and the client signature accepts it (`metacritic.py:866`). I swept the whole call surface: scheduler→`run_acquisition` (`scheduler.py:335-351` matches `pipeline.py:151-197`), pipeline→source factory (`pipeline.py:611` matches the source constructors), pipeline→`lookup_game` — no other mismatched kwarg remains.
- `pages_this_cycle += pages_scanned` now precedes the date-mode block (`pipeline.py:435-448`); the regression test at `test_pipeline.py:8891+` is non-vacuous (the pre-fix ordering leaves `pages_this_cycle == 0`, so `range_empty` resets and the seeded cursor assertion fails).
- `max_date` floor validation (≥1958, month 01–12, 0=off, future clamp) is real (`config.py:146-171`).
- `_effective_cutoff` compares parsed dates, not strings (`metacritic.py:982-1003`), covered by `test_effective_cutoff_compares_dates_not_strings`.
- Cache migration ordering/value preservation is real (`config.py:1040-1053`); `test_migration_runs_before_freegog_defaults_injection` would fail if the registration moved after the freegog injection (9 → 6), and `_upgrade_freegog_entry` only adds missing keys.
- Page-mode invariance holds: `cutoff_date=None`, `max_month_span=0`, same budget arithmetic, same log branch (`pipeline.py:392-399`, `pipeline.py:697-709`).

### Findings

1. **HIGH — `pipeline.py:387-390`** — With `max_cycle_months == 0` (“no month pacing”) the later-call branch still builds a pace cutoff: `subtract_months(max_month_seen, 0)` returns `max_month_seen` unchanged (`utils.py:210-213`), so `cutoff_date` becomes the first day of the newest month already seen. Every year below the anchor’s year is then entirely “before the cutoff”, the client stops on page 1 (`metacritic.py:932-940`), `cutoff_stopped` breaks the year loop (`pipeline.py:447-450`). Result: a date sweep advances **one year per cycle** instead of sweeping to the floor. This contradicts the README (`README.md:184`, “`0` = no month pacing”) and the spec (“`0` = no month pacing (sweep to the floor, watchdog permitting)”). Default `max_date: 202401` + default `max_cycle_months: 0` is the headline configuration, so the primary new feature is wrong out of the box. Repro: `_run(max_date=202401, max_cycle_months=0, scan_games=[{"release_date": "2025-11-05"}])` — the second call gets `cutoff_date == "2025-11-01"` instead of `"2024-01-01"`. **Fix:** `pipeline.py` — only compute `pace_month`/`max(...)` when `cfg.max_cycle_months > 0`; when it is 0, pass `cutoff_date = year_month_to_date(floor_month)` (absolute cutoff only, as the first call does).

2. **MEDIUM — `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:8768-8770`** — `test_no_month_span_when_pacing_disabled` claims “max_cycle_months 0 sweeps to the floor with no span limit” but only asserts `calls[0]["max_month_span"] == 0`. Because its mock returns no games, `max_month_seen` stays `None` and *every* call takes the first-call branch, so the test never exercises the later-call cutoff and would not fail if finding 1 returned. **Fix:** `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py` — return a game from the current year and assert every later call’s `cutoff_date == "2024-01-01"` (and `max_month_span == 0`).

3. **MEDIUM — `pipeline.py:520-531`** — A date-mode cycle that legitimately ends on a date cutoff with no collected games can send a false scrape-failure notification. `drained` is taken from the **last** scan call’s `_recent_games_exhausted`; a cutoff stop leaves that flag `False` (`metacritic.py:611`, `metacritic.py:930-940`), and `cached_exists` probes only the all-time key and the current year’s page 1, neither of which is generally cached in date mode (year-scoped keys, 6 h TTL). This branch fires in the cycle that reaches a mid-year floor boundary and ends with `pages_this_cycle == 0` + `drained_probes > 0` (the same cycle that logs “Backlog complete” and resets). `_check_scrape_health()` returns `metacritic_broken` whenever the site responds, so users with Apprise configured get “Metacritic browse returned no games — the site structure may have changed.” on a healthy site. **Fix:** `pipeline.py` — treat `cutoff_stopped` (a deliberate date bound) as an expected empty result, e.g. `drained = not fetch_failed and (exhausted is True or cutoff_stopped)`.

4. **MEDIUM — `pipeline.py:464` (test: `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:8786-8805`)** — `at_floor = cutoff_stopped and min_month_seen <= floor_month` needs a *collected* game dated at/before the floor month. The loop stops at the floor **year** and the browse listing is year-scoped (`metacritic.py:807-820`), so for a `YYYY01` floor the floor year’s pages can never be “all before” the floor and `cutoff_stopped` is never set in that cycle; the reset silently falls through to `range_empty` one cycle later (extra probe cycle, and the false notification from finding 3). The new test pins `cutoff_reached=True` together with a `2023-12-15` game on a scan whose `year` is the current year — a state the real client cannot produce — so the real completion boundary (floor-year exhaustion) is untested. **Fix:** `pipeline.py` — treat “floor year drained in this cycle” (or “the effective cutoff that bound the last call equals the floor”) as `at_floor`; update `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py` to cover a January floor and an exhausted floor year.

5. **MEDIUM — `README.md:322-324`** — After the new text “In date mode … both page keys are unused”, the paragraph keeps the unqualified sentence “The scanner advances through the `max_pages` window progressively — each cycle resumes where the last one left off, with auto-reset to page 1 when the `max_pages` budget is exhausted.” In date mode the scanner advances through year cursors and resets on backlog completion, so the paragraph now contradicts itself. **Fix:** `README.md` — scope that sentence to page mode (or move it above the date-mode sentence).

6. **LOW — `config.py:990` (log text at `config.py:299/306`)** — `_rename_source_cache_hours` passes the source name as `_rename_config_key`’s `platform_key`, so migration INFO lines read “Config: migrated 'cache_pages_hours'→'cache_hours' for platform 'fitgirl'”. **Fix:** `config.py` — pass a source-oriented label, or add a `label` parameter to `_rename_config_key`.

7. **LOW — `tests/unit/test_metacritic.py:5-11`** — `Any` is now imported twice (module level and inside `if TYPE_CHECKING`). With `from __future__ import annotations` the module-level import is unnecessary; a ruff/autoflake pass may rewrite it. **Fix:** `tests/unit/test_metacritic.py` — keep one import.

**Blockers only note:** none of the round-1 HIGH fixes regressed; the new blocker is finding 1.

1. **MEDIUM — `src/gamarr/pipeline.py:387-388` (later-call pace branch): `max_cycle_months == 0` produces an accidental hard cutoff at the cycle-anchor month instead of no pace.** What is wrong: on every call after the first in a date-mode cycle, the code computes `pace_month = subtract_months(max_month_seen, cfg.max_cycle_months)` and passes `cutoff_date = max(year_month_to_date(pace_month), year_month_to_date(floor_month))`. With `max_cycle_months = 0`, `subtract_months` deliberately returns the input unchanged (`utils.py:200-216`, "months <= 0 returns year_month unchanged"), so the later call's cutoff becomes the first day of the **anchor month itself**. Any later call therefore stops on its first page (the next year's listing is entirely older than the anchor month). Why it matters: `0` is documented as "`0` = no month pacing" (README.md:184, config model default) and the design spec pins it explicitly: `docs/agent/specs/2026-11-06-max-date-backlog-cutoff-design.md:170-171` — `target_month = max(floor_month, cycle_start - max_cycle_months)` with the comment `# max_cycle_months == 0 -> target_month = floor_month`. A user setting `max_date` spanning several years with `max_cycle_months: 0` gets a sweep that advances one year per cycle (plus one wasted boundary fetch per cycle) instead of sweeping to the floor in one cycle — the very configuration a user picks to drain a deep backlog "with no pacing". Results are eventually correct (the following cycle's first call has `max_month_seen is None` and uses the floor), no data loss, but it is a real spec/behavior contradiction with zero test coverage: `test_no_month_span_when_pacing_disabled` (test_pipeline.py:8768-8771) runs with no collected games, so the later-call branch never activates; `test_later_calls_use_the_cycle_anchor_not_a_fresh_span` only tests mcm=2. 2. **LOW — `src/gamarr/metacritic.py:471-489` (`_page_is_before_cutoff`): a page that mixes undated games with dated-below-cutoff games counts as "all before cutoff" and is skipped, so undated games on the stopping page are never collected.** What is wrong: `all(_is_before_date(...) for g in games if g.get("release_date") is not None)` excludes undated games from the check; only a page with **zero** dated games is kept ("unknown age — keep page"). This helper is pre-existing, but before this change the pipeline never passed a real `cutoff_date`, so the branch was dead in production; date mode makes it live. Why it matters: a game on the floor-year boundary page without a parseable release date is permanently invisible (the sweep re-stops at the same page every cycle after the floor reset). Its dated neighbours are below the user's explicit floor, so the impact is contained to an in-listing undated item interleaved with below-floor games — defensible semantics, but undocumented ("unknown age" is only honoured for fully-undated pages) and untested for the mixed case. Fix would live in `src/gamarr/metacritic.py` (make a partially-undated page un-stoppable, or document the mixed-page rule) plus a pin test in `tests/unit/test_metacritic.py`.

3. **LOW — `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`:8786-8817 (`test_date_mode_resets_progress_at_floor`): the `at_floor` boundary comparator is not pinned.** The trigger game is `2023-12-15` against floor `202401` — strictly below the floor. If the comparison at `pipeline.py:463` regressed directionally (`min_month_seen > floor_month` instead of `<=`, or operands swapped), this test still passes; only a game **at** the floor month (e.g. `2024-01-05` with floor `202401`) would be mis-reset. Why it matters: the reset contract ("sweep back to and **including** this month", README.md:183) is exactly the `<=` edge. Fix: extend the test in `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py` with a floor-month-dated game, or parameterize the floor-month/non-floor-month pair.

4. **LOW — `docs/agent/specs/2026-11-06-max-date-backlog-cutoff-design.md:212-215` vs `src/gamarr/pipeline.py:456-476`: the spec says the sweep completes "when the floor year finishes, either by listing exhaustion or by the cutoff stop … That calls db.reset_progress()", but the implementation resets in-cycle only on the cutoff stop.** A floor year that ends by listing exhaustion (e.g. `max_date: 202401`, the 2024 listing physically runs out — no page is ever all-before the floor) leaves `cutoff_stopped` False, so `at_floor` is False and the reset happens one cycle later via `range_empty`. The behaviour is safe (matches page-mode's drained-reset precedent — nothing wanted is lost, and the deferred reset is what the page-mode code already does), but the spec sentence over-promises. Smallest fix: update the design-doc line to say the exhaustion case completes via the next cycle's all-drained re-probe, or extend `at_floor` to also accept a confirmed floor-year exhaustion in the same cycle (pipeline change + test). Note this also interacts with finding 1: it is one more source of the "one extra cycle before restart" visible under `max_cycle_months: 0`.

Explicit severity accounting: **HIGH — no findings** (the two round‑1 HIGHs are verified fixed, and the drain/reset state machine has no remaining path that wipes per-year cursors ahead of unfetched wanted pages). **MEDIUM — 1 (finding 1 above).** **LOW — 3 (findings 2–4).**

1. The sweep eventually reaches 2024 with a fresh allowance. `max_month_seen` is `None` (all newer years probed empty), so `month_span_left = 2`; the client anchors on 2024 page 1 (Dec 2024) → effective cutoff `2024-10-01` → stops when a page is all older than Oct 2024 → `cutoff_reached=True`.
2. `scan_year == cutoff_year` → `floor_year_finished=True` → "Backlog complete — reached 2024-10 (floor 2024-01), restarting from the newest year" → `reset_progress`.
3. Next cycle re-scans 2026 from page 1. Every time the sweep gets back to 2024 it stops at Oct 2024 and resets again.

The worst case is a floor in the *current* year (`max_date: 202601`, `max_cycle_months: 2`): `cutoff_year == current_year`, so the cycle is a single year, the anchor is always page 1 of that year, and the sweep is permanently stuck on the newest two months — it never advances at all.

    def _run_floor_cycle(

        floor_year = floor_month // 100
        mock_mc = MagicMock()

            scan_year = kwargs.get("year")
            start_page = kwargs.get("start_page", 1)
            mock_mc._recent_games_failed = fetch_fails
            if scan_year == floor_year:
                mock_mc._recent_games_cutoff_reached = stop_cutoff is not None
                mock_mc._recent_games_stop_cutoff = stop_cutoff
                if floor_games:
                    mock_mc._recent_games_exhausted = False
                    mock_mc._recent_games_last_page = start_page
                    return floor_games
                mock_mc._recent_games_exhausted = stop_cutoff is None and not fetch_fails
                mock_mc._recent_games_last_page = start_page - 1

            mock_mc._recent_games_cutoff_reached = False
            mock_mc._recent_games_stop_cutoff = None
            mock_mc._recent_games_exhausted = False
            mock_mc._recent_games_last_page = start_page
            return [{"title": f"G{scan_year}", "slug": f"g{scan_year}", "release_date": f"{scan_year}-06-01"}]

        mock_mc._recent_games_failed = False

        mock_mc._recent_games_stop_cutoff = None

    def test_date_mode_resets_progress_at_floor(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """A stop at the ABSOLUTE floor in the floor year resets the cursors.

        A June floor is used because a January floor can never be met by an
        all-before-floor page inside its own year (that path is exhaustion).
        """
        from gamarr.database import Database

        path = str(tmp_path / "floor.db")
        self._run_floor_cycle(
            path=path,
            floor_month=202406,
            floor_games=[{"title": "Floor", "slug": "floor", "release_date": "2024-05-20"}],
            stop_cutoff="2024-06-01",

## Review

I read the full current `src/gamarr/{config,metacritic,pipeline,scheduler,utils}.py`, the changed test files, and the README table/step-level docs. I have no shell, so this is based on `watchdog_diff` (working tree vs HEAD) plus the current file contents; I could not execute the suite (commands at the end).

### Correct (round‑3 fixes verified against the code, not the summary)

- **Stop-cause signal is per-call, not stale.** `scan_recent_games` clears `_recent_games_cutoff_reached` *and* `_recent_games_stop_cutoff` at the top of every call (`metacritic.py:923-928`), `_classify_page` never touches them, and the only writer is `metacritic.py:948-950` on a stop. The pipeline reads them immediately after the call, inside the try. No stale-read path found.
- **Page mode never consults it.** The only readers are `pipeline.py:450` and `pipeline.py:461`, both inside `if date_mode:`. In page mode `cutoff_date=None` ⇒ `_effective_cutoff` returns `None` ⇒ `_page_is_before_cutoff` returns `False`, so `cutoff_stopped` can never become True and `pipeline.py:539`'s suppression is unchanged for page mode. Page-mode call shape is pinned by `test_page_mode_call_shape_has_no_date_arguments`.
- **Effective-cutoff == floor on the first paced call is correct, not a false positive.** `_effective_cutoff` returns the caller's `cutoff_date` *verbatim* when `span_parsed <= cutoff_parsed` (`metacritic.py:1006-1020`), so the string compare at `pipeline.py:461` matches exactly the ISO floor the client was given; and if the effective cutoff *is* the floor, a page of all-before-floor games genuinely means the sweep reached `max_date`.
- **Pace stop no longer resets.** `floor_stop` is now cause-based; `test_pace_stop_in_floor_year_keeps_cursors` genuinely pins it (the old `cutoff_reached and scan_year == cutoff_year` form would reset the 2024 cursor to 0 and fail the assertion).
- **Pacing wiring is coherent.** First call → `max_month_span=N, cutoff=floor`; later calls → `max(floor, max_month_seen−N)` with `max_month_span=0` (`pipeline.py:378-392`). Because the first page of a call always contains the anchor, a page‑1 cutoff stop on a first call is arithmetically impossible, so the resume-page anchor cannot deadlock the sweep; the loop breaks (never resets) on `cutoff_stopped`.
- **README is accurate for the new keys** — `max_date` clamping, month validation, the `max()` (floor always wins) rule, and the "N+1 calendar months at a boundary" caveat all match `config.py:129-164` / `pipeline.py:387-388` / `metacritic.py:1006-1020`. Migration ordering comment is correct: `_migrate_platform_overrides` and `_migrate_fitgirl_cache_ttl_hours` run before `_migrate_cache_pages_hours_to_cache_hours`, which runs before the freegog injection, so `cache_ttl_hours → cache_pages_hours → cache_hours` resolves in one load; `test_migration_runs_before_freegog_defaults_injection` is non-vacuous (reversing the order yields 6, not 9).

### Findings

1. **MEDIUM** — `src/gamarr/pipeline.py:433-437`. A fetch failure that happens *mid-year* (`pages_scanned > 0`) never sets `fetch_failed`, because `_recent_games_failed` is only read inside `if pages_scanned == 0:`. The client does set the flag for any failed page (`metacritic.py:613-616`).     tree = ast.parse(cur)
    lines = cur.split("\n")
    cls = next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == cls_name)
    fns = [f for f in cls.body if isinstance(f, ast.FunctionDef)]
    have = [f.name for f in fns]

    blocks = {}
    for f in fns:
        start = f.lineno - 1
        for dec in getattr(f, "decorator_list", []):
            start = min(start, dec.lineno - 1)
        blocks[f.name] = "\n".join(lines[start:f.end_lineno])

The descent is bounded by `range(current_year, cutoff_year - 1, -1)` (:367) — **no unbounded descent and no infinite intra-cycle loop**; the only residual is Finding 2 below.
- **Round-4 LOW fixes.** `_classify_page(cancel_event: CancelSignal | None)` (metacritic.py:604); `_page_limit_reached` is the sole owner of the page budget (metacritic.py:1030-1055) with the cutoff predicate evaluated once (:1015); the "max_cycle_months ignored because max_date is not set" log exists (pipeline.py:312-313); `test_year_loop_stops_when_the_allowance_is_already_spent` (:9118) pins the guard; `tests/unit/test_database.py` shows no delta.

- **Pacing branch analysis.** First call: anchor = newest month of the first page ⇒ page 1 can never trigger the pace cutoff (the anchor is derived from it), so no zero-progress re-anchor stall. Later calls: `cutoff = max(anchor − N, floor)` with `anchor = max_month_seen` (a monotone max over the cycle), which equals the client's own span cutoff and is strictly older each cycle — no gap, no overshoot past the floor. `subtract_months`/`_month_span`/`year_month_to_date` arithmetic checks out at year boundaries (202501−1=202412, 202601−2=202511).

The skipped year's cursor never advances (`pages_scanned == 0`), so it is re-probed (one fetch) and re-skipped every cycle forever, and its in-range games are never collected. **Why it matters:** this is the exact "wrong completion" residual the round-4 change traded for the stall; a mis-indexed/truncated listing now silently loses a whole year of the backlog instead of stalling loudly. 3. **LOW — `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:6976` with `test_failed_browse_fetch_does_not_reset_progress` at `:7294-7318`.** The round-4 change replaced `mock_mc._recent_games_failed = fetch_fails` with a hard-coded `False`, so `fetch_fails=True` now only suppresses `_recent_games_exhausted`. The pipeline therefore never sees a failure: the test passes for the "stalled probe" reason even if the `fetch_failed` guard were deleted, contradicting its docstring ("A failed fetch is not a drained year"). The page-mode guard's only distinguishing scenario (one year drained + one year failed) is untested. **Fix:** set `_recent_games_failed = fetch_fails` and give the test a drained year plus a failed year (as `test_fetch_failure_is_still_reported_as_a_scrape_failure` does for the notify path). **File:** `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`.

## Review

**Correct**

- **Page-mode invariance with `max_date == 0`.** `date_mode` is false, so the client still receives `cutoff_date=None`, `max_month_span=0`, the unchanged page allowance, and `_games_at_or_after_floor` is never called (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:311-313`, `366-389`, `426-435`, `450-451`, `517-518`). `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:9108-9121` asserts the call shape.
- **Round-6 exhaustion fix is present.** `_classify_page` uses `page_number > 1` (`src/gamarr/metacritic.py:630`); a fresh scan that walks pages 1..N and probes N+1 now reports exhaustion, while an empty page 1 does not. Page-mode reset still requires a zero-page probe (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:470-473`, `528-530`), so the page-mode drained-reset semantics are unchanged. `TestCutoffReachedFlag` covers both fresh and resumed cases.
- **Floor filter is correctly scoped.** `_games_at_or_after_floor` keeps undated games and applies month-grain `>=` (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:112-129`), is called only in date mode (`:450-451`), and is unit-tested (`tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:9233-9249`).
- **Floor stop vs pace stop is distinguished.** The client records the effective cutoff (`src/gamarr/metacritic.py:956-958`), and the pipeline compares it with `floor_cutoff` (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:492-500`). `test_drained_year_then_cutoff_year_does_not_reset_progress` models a reachable pace cutoff (anchor 2025-11, span 2 → 2025-09) and keeps cursors.
- **`max_date` config validation and future clamp** are implemented with the documented bounds and warning (`src/gamarr/config.py:121-163`), and `run_acquisition`'s integer validation precedence is correct (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:218`).
- **Cache-key migration** covers both owners, every mapping body of a multi-source `download_sites` entry, and runs before the freegog defaults injection (`src/gamarr/config.py:960-1006`, `1059-1068`). `TestCacheHoursRename` is non-vacuous, including the RED-verified multi-key and ordering tests (`tests/unit/test_config.py:1828-1928`).

**Findings**

1. **MEDIUM — a transient empty page mid-listing can falsely complete a date sweep and reset all cursors.**
   `src/gamarr/metacritic.py:630` sets `_recent_games_exhausted` for *any* empty page past page 1, but `_fetch_browse_page` deliberately never caches empty parses because "a transient empty page must not be replayed" (`src/gamarr/metacritic.py:816-821`). Page mode is shielded by the `pages_scanned == 0` guard (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:470-473`, `529`), but date mode sets `floor_year_finished` from `_recent_games_exhausted` regardless of pages scanned (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:496-500`), then `sweep_complete` resets every progress row and logs "Backlog complete" (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:528-537`). An empty page 7 of the floor year therefore wipes the sweep state even though pages 8+ may contain in-floor games; a repeatable pagination gap would permanently skip them. This is the exact transient-empty risk the round-6 `page_number > 1` change leaves open for fresh scans.
   *Smallest fix:* confirm a drain once before setting the flag (re-probe the empty page/page+1), or have the pipeline treat exhaustion as floor completion only after a confirming zero-page probe. Add a test with an empty page N and a non-empty page N+1 in the floor year. Files: `src/gamarr/metacritic.py` (and/or `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`).

2. **MEDIUM — the pace-stop test asserts an unreachable client state and would pass with pacing broken.**
   `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:8952-8971` runs `_run_floor_cycle(max_cycle_months=25)`. With the fake's 2026-06 anchor, `subtract_months(202606, 25)` is 202405, which is older than the 202406 floor, so the pipeline passes `cutoff_date="2024-06-01"` and `max_month_span=0` to the floor-year call (`src/gamarr/pipeline.py:415-425`). The fake nevertheless reports `stop_cutoff="2024-09-01"` (`tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:8818-8830`), a value the real client cannot return because it reports the effective cutoff it was given. With a realistic fake that echoes `kwargs["cutoff_date"]`, this scenario is a *floor* stop and the sweep completes, contradicting the test's expectation. The reachable floor-year pace stop is the floor year being the first call with games (`max_month_seen is None` → `month_span_left=N`), or a derived cutoff newer than the floor.
   *Smallest fix:* seed the newer years as drained probes so the floor year is the first call with games, use a pace that yields a cutoff newer than the floor, and have the fake copy `kwargs["cutoff_date"]` into `_recent_games_stop_cutoff`. File: `tests/unit/test_pipeline.py`.

3. **MEDIUM — the round-6 `run_acquisition` normalisation is untested.**

def _effective_page_cap(max_games: int) -> int:
    """Return the per-call game cap, treating 0 as unlimited.

    Args:
        max_games: The caller's cap; 0 or negative means unlimited.

    Returns:
        A large sentinel when unlimited, otherwise *max_games*.
    """
    return max_games if max_games > 0 else 999999


def _page_newest_month(games: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int | None:
    """Return the newest release month (``YYYYMM``) on a browse page.

    Args:
        games: The parsed games of one browse page.

    Returns:
        The newest ``YYYYMM`` month, or ``None`` when no page entry has one.
    """
    months = [month for month in (month_of(g.get("release_date")) for g in games) if month is not None]
    return max(months) if months else None


def _effective_cutoff(cutoff_date: str | None, span_anchor: int | None, max_month_span: int) -> str | None:
    """Return the newer of the absolute cutoff and the month-span cutoff.

    Args:
        cutoff_date: The caller's absolute date floor, if any.
        span_anchor: The newest month of this call's first page, if known.
        max_month_span: Months of pacing; 0 disables the span cutoff.

    Returns:
        The effective cutoff date string, or ``None`` when there is no date stop.
    """
    if max_month_span <= 0 or span_anchor is None:
        return cutoff_date
    span_cutoff = year_month_to_date(subtract_months(span_anchor, max_month_span))
    if cutoff_date is None:
        return span_cutoff
    # Compare parsed dates, not strings: cutoff_date may be DD-MM-YYYY.
    cutoff_parsed = _parse_date_flexible(cutoff_date)
    span_parsed = _parse_date_flexible(span_cutoff)
    if cutoff_parsed is None or span_parsed is None or span_parsed > cutoff_parsed:
        return span_cutoff
    return cutoff_date


def _page_stop_decision(
    sort_order: str,
    games: list[dict[str, Any]],
    cutoff_date: str | None,
    max_month_span: int,
    span_anchor: int | None,
    max_pages: int,
    page_number: int,
    start_page: int,
) -> tuple[bool, bool, str | None]:
    """Decide whether a browse page ends the scan and whether a date caused it.

    Args:
        sort_order: The active browse order.
        games: The parsed games of the current page.
        cutoff_date: The caller's absolute date floor, if any.
        max_month_span: Months of pacing; 0 disables the span cutoff.
        span_anchor: The newest month of this call's first page, if known.
        max_pages: Per-call page limit; 0 disables it.
        page_number: The page just fetched.
        start_page: The page this call started from.

    Returns:
        ``(should_stop, cutoff_reached, effective_cutoff)``.  The third element
        lets the caller tell *which* date bound stopped the page: the caller's
        absolute floor or a month-span (pace) bound derived from its own anchor.
    """
    effective_cutoff = _effective_cutoff(cutoff_date, span_anchor, max_month_span)
    # Evaluate the date predicate once: it is both the "cutoff reached" signal
    # and one of the two stop conditions.
    cutoff_reached = sort_order == "new" and _page_is_before_cutoff(games, effective_cutoff)
    if cutoff_reached:
        logger.debug(
            "Metacritic page {} reached (all games older than {}); stopping scan",
            page_number,
            effective_cutoff,
        )
    stop = cutoff_reached or _page_limit_reached(max_pages, page_number, start_page)
    return stop, cutoff_reached, effective_cutoff


def _log_scan_result(year: int | None, pages_fetched: int, game_count: int) -> None:
    """Log the outcome of one browse scan, naming the year when there is one."""
    if year is not None:
        logger.info("Scan result for {}: {} pages browsed, {} games collected", year, pages_fetched, game_count)
    else:
        logger.info("Scan result: {} pages browsed, {} games collected", pages_fetched, game_count)


def _page_limit_reached(max_pages: int, page_number: int, start_page: int) -> bool:
    """Return True when the per-call page limit has been reached.

    Date stops are owned by :func:`_page_stop_decision`, which evaluates the
    cutoff predicate once; this helper only covers the page budget.

    Args:
        max_pages: Per-call page limit; 0 disables it.
        page_number: The page just fetched.
        start_page: The page this call started from.

    Returns:
        True when the limit is spent.
    """
    if max_pages > 0 and (page_number - start_page) >= max_pages:
        logger.debug(
            "Metacritic page limit {} reached (max_pages={}); stopping scan",
            page_number - start_page,
            max_pages,
        )
        return True
    return False


def _log_batch_progress(page_number: int, game_count: int, show_progress: bool) -> None:
    """Log periodic scan progress when *show_progress* is True."""
    if page_number % 100 == 0 and show_progress:
        logger.info(
            "Backlog scan: page {} ({} games)",
            page_number,
            game_count,
        )

## Review

Round 8, verified from the actual working-tree diff (`src/`, `tests/`, `README.md`) and the current files. No HIGH finding.

**Round‑7 fixes re-verified (not taken on trust):**
- Drain confirmation (`metacritic.py:938-944`) is real: `_fetch_browse_page` only caches when `if parsed:` (`metacritic.py:815-819`), so the re-probe is a genuine fetch for an empty parse; `_classify_page(None, …)` sets `_recent_games_failed`, so an empty‑then‑failed probe is *not* read as a drain.
- **Cache-hit accounting is unaffected**: `cache_hits` is incremented only on *detail* cache hits (`metacritic.py:696-699`), never for browse pages — the extra probe cannot skew `_log_batch_summary`.
- **No page arithmetic double-count**: `pages_fetched`/`_recent_games_last_page` derive from `page_number`, not fetch count (`metacritic.py:975-981`); `_page_limit_reached` counts `page_number - start_page`; `per_call_max`/`remaining_pages` are decremented only in page mode (`pipeline.py:543`). The probe adds requests but no budget.
- Floor/pace distinction is real and pinned: `_recent_games_stop_cutoff` is the *effective* cutoff (`metacritic.py:958-961`, `1030`), compared to `floor_cutoff` at `pipeline.py:517`; the fake in `test_pace_stop_in_floor_year_keeps_cursors` reports span‑vs‑given exactly as `_effective_cutoff` does, and the state it models (page 1 collected → later page trips the span) *is* reachable.
- Normalisation/`_month_span`/`_games_at_or_after_floor` assertions, the mis‑indexed‑year warning, and the removed dead `start_page` parameter are all present as claimed. Page‑mode invariance holds (`cutoff_date=None`, `max_month_span=0`, identical allowance arithmetic, budget branch intact).

### Findings

1. **MEDIUM** — `src/gamarr/metacritic.py:497` + `src/gamarr/pipeline.py:112-132`: an undated game sitting on the page that trips the floor cutoff is never queued, which contradicts `_games_at_or_after_floor`'s documented policy ("Undated games are kept because their age is unknown"). `_page_is_before_cutoff` deliberately counts a page that mixes below‑cutoff dated games with undated ones as *before* the cutoff (docstring + `test_mixed_undated_and_old_page_counts_as_before_cutoff`), and `scan_recent_games` breaks *before* `all_games.extend(page[...])` (`metacritic.py:962-966`), so the whole page — undated entries included — is discarded before the pipeline's filter can see it. Because a completed sweep resets the cursors and the next sweep stops on the same page again, the loss is *sticky* at the floor boundary whenever `max_date` month ≥ 02 (a January floor ends by exhaustion, so its last page is kept). Why it matters: a TBA/undated title near the floor is silently never reviewed, exactly the class of game the filter says it protects. Smallest fix: correct `_games_at_or_after_floor`'s docstring to state that the stopping page is discarded whole (doc-only, `pipeline.py`), or collect the stopping page's undated entries in `scan_recent_games` when `cutoff_reached` (behaviour change, `metacritic.py`) — do *not* relax `_page_is_before_cutoff` to "any undated ⇒ before the cutoff", which would remove the stop entirely for listings containing undated entries.

2. **MEDIUM** — `src/gamarr/metacritic.py:1025 (`_effective_cutoff`): the span cutoff wins even when it is *unparsable*, silently dropping a valid absolute floor. `subtract_months` has no lower bound (`utils.py:199-218`) and `max_cycle_months` has no upper bound (`config.py:121`, `ge=0` only); with `max_cycle_months` ≳ 24 000 (or an all‑junk release-date page making `span_anchor` tiny) `year_month_to_date(...)` yields `"0000-01-01"`/`"-001-11-01"`, `_parse_date_flexible` returns `None`, and the `span_parsed is None` branch returns the unparsable span. The pipeline's first call of the cycle passes `max_month_span` (`pipeline.py:437-449`), so that call loses its `cutoff_date` floor and scans to the 2000‑page cap; `floor_stop` can then never fire for a single‑year range. Why it matters: fragile assumption on a user-supplied integer with silent loss of the "floor always wins" contract. Smallest fix: in `_effective_cutoff`, `if span_parsed is None: return cutoff_date` (and optionally `le=` on `max_cycle_months` in `config.py`). File: `src/gamarr/metacritic.py` (+ `config.py` if bounded).

3. **LOW** — `src/gamarr/pipeline.py:225-226`: the second `if isinstance(max_date, bool): max_date = 0` is dead code. `True` is already caught (and zeroed) by the block above because it is truthy and hits `isinstance(max_date, bool)`; `False` is already falsy. Harmless, but it reads as if a case were still unhandled. File: `src/gamarr/pipeline.py`.

4. **LOW** — `tests/unit/test_metacritic.py` (class `TestCutoffReachedFlag`) has no test for the new confirmation path's failure mode: first probe empty → confirmation probe returns `None` must set `_recent_games_failed` and *not* `_recent_games_exhausted`. `test_transient_empty_page_is_not_read_as_a_drain` only covers empty→games, and `test_exhausted_listing_does_not_set_flag` covers the non-probed `start_page>1` path. ### Findings

1. **MEDIUM — pipeline.py:609–616 — the scrape-health gate still trusts an empty cached browse row, so the round-8 fix is only half-applied.** `cached_exists` uses `mc._cache.get_browse_page(...) is not None`; a cached `[]` returns `[]` (not `None`), so it counts as "we have cached browse data" and suppresses `_diagnose_and_notify_scrape`. That is exactly the empty row `_cache_scope_matches` now calls untrusted. **Why it matters:** a real scrape outage can go unreported (until the row's TTL expires / a successful fetch overwrites it). Precondition is narrow — a legacy empty row still within `cache_hours` — but the two code paths now disagree by construction. **Fix:** pipeline.py — apply the same scope rule (or a truthiness test) to both cache reads.

2. **MEDIUM — pipeline.py:563–564 — the date-mode completion reset is not covered for cancellation.** `sweep_complete` is gated by `not is_cancelled(cancel_event)` before the destructive `db.reset_progress(...)`, but no test exercises a cancel that lands after a floor-year result: the only date-mode cancel coverage is the pre-set-event loop break (test_pipeline.py:5716, page mode). Removing the gate would break no test, and a shutdown mid-sweep would wipe every per-year cursor, forcing a full re-sweep. **Fix:** tests/unit/test_pipeline.py — one date-mode test that sets the event inside the floor-year `fake_scan` and asserts `get_last_scanned_page` is unchanged.

3. **LOW — README.md:275 — stale "Within cutoff weeks?" node in the acquisition flowchart.** The diff rewrote the cutoff feature bullet and the step narrative to a date floor (README.md:24–28, 309–316), but the Mermaid diagram still shows a per-game "cutoff weeks" gate. **Why it matters:** the README is the only user-facing doc and now contradicts itself about the changed filtering behaviour. (The node predates this diff, but this doc update is where it should be swept up.) **Fix:** README.md.

4. **LOW — README.md:184 / config.py:126 — the `max_cycle_months` upper bound is undocumented.** The field now has `le=1200` (round-8 mitigation), so `max_cycle_months: 1201` is a config-load `ValidationError`, while the README row documents only "`0` = no month pacing". **Why it matters:** an advisory bound is presented as a hard validation error with no documentation for it (the `max_date` row, by contrast, documents its range). **Fix:** README.md (state the 1200-month cap) — or drop the cap and rely on the floor.

5. **LOW — pipeline.py:364–365 — the "max_pages ignored in date mode" INFO fires on every date-mode cycle even when the user never configured `max_pages`.** `max_pages` defaults to 500, so `if date_mode and cfg.max_pages:` is always true; the design says inert-key logs fire "only when a key is set and cannot apply". **Why it matters:** persistent misleading config noise on every cycle in the mode this change introduces. **Fix:** pipeline.py (compare against the raw/override config, or reword the line).

6. **LOW — tests/unit/test_pipeline.py:8807,8814,8835–8839 — `_run_floor_cycle`'s `stop_cutoff` parameter is dead and its docstring is false.** The fake reports `effective` regardless: when `floor_games` is empty `reached` is already `False`; when it is non-empty `reached` is already `True`. ## Summary of changes on branch `main`

**The feature — date-based backlog cutoff (`max_date`), additive to the page budget**

- **New config keys** `max_date` (`YYYYMM`, `0` = disabled, year ≥ 1958, a future month clamps with a warning, cap on the pace at 1200 months) and `max_cycle_months` (pace in date mode, `0` = none). Date mode engages only for `sort_order: new`; `max_pages`/`max_cycle_pages` keep driving the score modes, whose browse lists mix years and cannot take a date bound. Inert keys log once per cycle when set and unusable.
- **The cutoff is a real month floor, not a page guess.** `pipeline.py` now passes the `cutoff_date` the client has always supported but never received, so the sweep stops inside the boundary year at `max_date`; the year range comes from the floor (`max_date // 100`) instead of `ceil(max_pages / 52)`, and the page-budget arithmetic and its "reset to page 1" branch are skipped entirely in date mode.
- **Pacing is cycle-anchored.** The first call of a cycle passes a month span (the client anchors on its own first dated page); later calls pass an absolute cutoff derived from the cycle's anchor, so a new year's listing cannot re-anchor and overshoot. The floor always wins — the pace can only shorten a cycle.
- **Completion is cause-aware.** `MetacriticClient` reports *which* cutoff stopped a call, so a pace stop inside the floor year is never mistaken for completing the sweep (three successive review rounds found variants of that bug); completion also covers an exhausted floor year and a data-free floor year. A transient empty page is confirmed with one re-probe before it is believed, and a stale empty cached row no longer counts as browse data.
- **Queue honesty:** a mixed boundary page no longer queues games older than `max_date` (`_games_at_or_after_floor`, undated games kept), and a date-mode cycle that ends on its own cutoff no longer files a false "site structure may have changed" alert.
- **Rename `cache_pages_hours` → `cache_hours`** on both owners (Metacritic browse cache and each download source), migrated in place by `_migrate_cache_pages_hours_to_cache_hours`, registered *before* the freegog defaults injection so a user's legacy value survives. The client/source constructor kwargs keep their internal names deliberately.
- **Also in this diff:** a tech-debt pass (removed 2 redundant tests introduced by this change, extracted helpers so CRAP is ≤ 8.81 everywhere, docstring accuracy sweep), 6 pre-existing regression tests restored after review flagged their deletion, README rows/narrative/flowchart updated, and the review's residual ledger added.

cd /data/gamarr; git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat: add date-based backlog cutoff and rename cache_pages_hours

Add max_date (YYYYMM month floor, 0 = disabled) and max_cycle_months
(per-cycle pace) for sort_order "new", so the backlog cutoff is stated as
a date instead of a page count. Score-ordered browsing keeps the page
budget, since its listing mixes years and no page maps to a date.

- Date mode reuses the browse scan's cutoff_date early-stop, derives the
  year range from the floor and skips the page-budget arithmetic.
- Pacing is cycle-anchored: the first call passes a month span, later calls
  pass an absolute cutoff, and the floor always wins.
- The client reports which cutoff stopped a call, so a pace stop inside the
  floor year is never read as completing the sweep. Completion also covers
  an exhausted floor year and a data-free floor year, and a transient empty
  page is confirmed with one re-probe.
- Games below the floor are filtered out of the queue before insertion.
- Rename cache_pages_hours to cache_hours on both owners, migrated in place
  before the freegog defaults injection so legacy values survive.

Also includes a tech-debt pass (helper extraction, CRAP <= 8.81, docstring
accuracy), six restored pre-existing regression tests, and the code review's
residual ledger (REVIEW_GATE_STATUS: UNRESOLVED, 1 MEDIUM + 3 LOW applied
but not independently re-reviewed at the round cap).
EOF
echo "commit_exit=$?"; git log --oneline -1

content.text:
**Done — shipped as v3.3.0.**

## What was released

**Commits** (`v3.2.5 → v3.3.0`, 4 commits):
- `d17090c` docs: spec — date-based backlog cutoff (`max_date`) alongside page budget
- `3925f82` docs: plan — date-based backlog cutoff implementation
- `de1e9ef` feat: add date-based backlog cutoff and rename `cache_pages_hours`
- `0a5c742` chore: bump version to 3.3.0

**Diff stat:** 16 files, **+4417 / −183**. Code: `config.py` +146, `metacritic.py` +270, `pipeline.py` +355, `utils.py` +84, `scheduler.py` +6; tests +1735; README +42; plus the spec, plan and residual ledger.

**Release:** https://github.com/binhex/gamarr/releases/tag/v3.3.0 — target `main`, notes generated from `v3.2.5`, tag verified at `0a5c742` (= `origin/main`). Branch preserved locally and remotely; no worktree cleanup needed (normal repo).

## Disclosures

1. **This branch ships with review residuals — it is not review-clean.** `REVIEW_GATE_STATUS: UNRESOLVED` at the round-10 cap. Ledger committed in this release: `docs/agent/reviews/2026-11-06-max-date-backlog-cutoff-residuals.md` — **1 MEDIUM** (a data-free floor year completing the sweep, `pipeline.py:521-530`) and **3 LOW** (drained flag set before the cancel check; over-stated cache-scope comment; `max_month_span` docstring anchor), all applied but never independently re-reviewed. QA ran `CLEAN` over that marker, as the chain defines.

2. **`git push` reported a repository security signal I should not bury:** *"GitHub found 42 vulnerabilities on binhex/gamarr's default branch (1 critical, 15 high, 19 moderate, 7 low)"* — Dependabot's advisory view. My QA dependency audit (`uvx pip-audit`) returned "No known vulnerabilities found", so the two disagree; the likely cause is advisories in locked/transitive or dev-only packages that `pip-audit` resolved differently, or a broader advisory database on GitHub's side. Worth a look at https://github.com/binhex/gamarr/security/dependabot — it is a pre-existing repository condition, not introduced by this change, but treating it as "clean" because my scanner said so would be wrong.

3. Version bump rationale: **MINOR** rather than PATCH — genuinely new public config surface (`max_date`, `max_cycle_months`) and behaviour; not MAJOR because the `cache_pages_hours` → `cache_hours` rename auto-migrates existing configs.

def _title_contains_keywords(title: str, keywords: list[str] | None) -> str | None:
    """Return the first matching keyword (lowercased), or None if no match."""
    if not keywords:
        return None
    title_lower = title.lower()
    for kw in keywords:
        if kw.lower() in title_lower:
            return kw.lower()
    return None


def _title_matches_reject(title: str, reject_title: list[str] | None) -> bool:
=== where the article-body check happens ===
def _check_reject_keywords(
    db: Database,
    best: dict[str, Any],
    game_title: str,
    game_slug: str,
    reject_keywords: list[str] | None,
) -> bool:
    """Check whether a match should be skipped due to rejected keywords.

    Returns True if the match should be skipped, keeping the game
    pending for the next cycle.  Fetches the FitGirl HTML page and
    checks the **article body** first (most descriptive), then the
    HTML ``<title>`` tag, against *reject_keywords*.  When the page
    cannot be fetched, the match is kept pending for re-check in the
    next cycle (the sitemap title is too weak a signal).

    The check is deliberately scoped to the ``<article>`` element to
    exclude sidebar navigation (which contains "Hypervisor" links on
    every page) and the comments section (rogue comments should never
    block a download).  Article text is additionally truncated before
    the "Backwards Compatibility" section to avoid false positives from
    historical references to previous repacks.
    """
    if not reject_keywords:
        return False

    # Single HTTP request for both title and article body
    page_title, article_text = _fetch_fitgirl_page_content(best["url"])

    if page_title is None and article_text is None:
        # Cannot verify reject_keywords against the page content.
        # Erring on the side of caution — keep game pending so it can
        # be re-checked in the next cycle when the page may be reachable.
        logger.warning(
            "Could not fetch page content for '{}' \u2014 keeping '{}' pending for re-check",
            best["url"],
            game_title,
        )
        db.touch_pending(game_slug)
        return True

    # Truncate article text before "Backwards Compatibility" section.
    # FitGirl pages describe backwards compatibility with previous repacks
    # there, which may reference keywords (e.g. "HV", "hypervisor") from
    # older releases — causing false positives for current non-HV repacks.
    article_text = _truncate_at_backwards_compat(article_text)

    if article_text and (matched := _title_contains_keywords(article_text, reject_keywords)):
        logger.info(
            "Skipping match for '{}' \u2014 FitGirl article body contains rejected keyword '{}'",
            game_title,
            matched,
        )
        db.touch_pending(game_slug)
        return True

content.text:
I've traced this end-to-end: your live database, the daemon logs, and the code paths that produce those lines. Short version: **the code is doing what it was built to do, but three things make it not do what you want** — and one of them explains the missing downloads almost entirely.

## What gamarr actually does today

Discovery is **Metacritic-first, always**:

1. Browse Metacritic PC releases in `sort_order` (`new` = newest release date first, per year).
2. Filter at browse time (`reject_title`, genre, review counts), queue survivors into `pending_games`.
3. Verify each queued game against its Metacritic **detail page** (real 0–100 / 0–10 scores).
4. Only then search FitGirl/FreeGOG for a match and deliver.

So **"latest games on FitGirl/FreeGOG → check Metacritic"** — your mode 2 — **does not exist**. The sources are never enumerated on their own; they are only searched for titles Metacritic already handed over. A brand-new repack for a game Metacritic hasn't surfaced is invisible, no matter how new it is.

Your mode 1 (backlog) exists in the sense that a date/page window is swept and each hit is looked up on the sources — but it is a *Metacritic* crawl, not a source-catalogue crawl. And your mode 3 (`sort_order: criticscore` / `userscore`) exists, but it is **order-only, not filtering**, and it has no year dimension, which is precisely why `max_date` is ignored in those modes.

## Why nothing downloads — the main defect

Your live log, ~18 days (867 cycles): **10,409 match attempts were skipped by `reject_keywords`**, and 7,821 of those were the two-letter token **`hv`**:

```
Skipping match for 'Black Myth: Wukong'      — FitGirl article body contains rejected keyword 'hv'
Skipping match for 'Metaphor: ReFantazio'    — ... 'hv'
Skipping match for 'Resident Evil Requiem'   — ... 'hv'
Skipping match for 'Forza Horizon 6'         — ... 'hypervisor'
Skipping match for 'Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds' — ... 'emulator'
```

`_title_contains_keywords` is a **plain case-insensitive substring test** over the whole FitGirl article body. I fetched a real page to see what it hits: the Wukong article contains *"Only updated files for a new **non-HV** repack"* and *"convert your INSTALLED **HV** version"* → the word `hv` appears in **conversion-patch notes**, so a legitimate non-HV repack is rejected.

Result: **all 21 games that passed Metacritic verification** — Wukong, Metaphor, RE Requiem, Forza Horizon 6, Crimson Desert, Jurassic World Evolution 3 — are blocked. All-time history: **63 delivered, 9,490 failed, 16,896 expired.**

## Why you see older games, sporadically

- The queue is 1,555 pending, of which **1,534 were checked and kept as "below thresholds"** — they sit for 30 days and mostly expire en masse (you can see 276 expired on Oct 30, 110 on Nov 1).
- The 2026 sweep has cached **866 pages** and runs at `max_cycle_months: 1` (≈16 pages/cycle), so a cycle mostly re-walks pages whose slugs are already known — log line: *"3 of 800 collected games passed title/age filters"*. Dedupe means a game is processed once, ever.
- What *does* slip through is often a 2024/2025 title that was queued weeks earlier and finally matched — hence bursts, no pattern. The last delivery batch (28 on Nov 5) was FF XVI, Dragon Ball Sparking! Zero, Red Dead Redemption, Romancing SaGa 2 — all ~2024.
- `max_date` is currently `202601` and `max_cycle_months: 1`. At 19:22 the log shows `Backlog complete — reached no pages (floor 2026-01)` → the 2026 sweep hit the end of its listing and reset; it will now crawl from page 1 again at ~16 pages per 30-minute cycle.

So: the sweep is spending nearly all its time on noise, the good candidates are killed by a substring, and the only mode that could have found "what's new on FitGirl" doesn't exist.

## What needs changing (no code written)

| # | Problem | Options |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `hv` / `emulator` substring rejects real non-HV repacks | word-boundary matching + ignore negations ("non-HV"), or check the repack **title** only, or drop `hv` |
| 2 | No source-first "latest" mode | new mode: enumerate FitGirl sitemap / FreeGOG A-Z for repacks published in the last N days, then fetch Metacritic scores for those titles and apply thresholds |
| 3 | Backlog mode crawls noise; queue is a graveyard | tighten pre-queue filtering (real score threshold before queueing), cap queue size, shorter expiry for below-threshold entries |
| 4 | `sort_order` is order-only, no filtering | decide whether critic/user score should also *filter* at browse time (it can't — browse scores are internal metrics — so it must filter at verification) |
| 5 | Modes are implicit | make "backlog" vs "latest" an explicit run mode rather than a consequence of `max_date`/window settings |

Four questions to pin down the target behaviour before anything is changed:

options.description: You do want to skip hypervisor/VM-only repacks, but the current plain-substring test is wrong: it fires on conversion-patch notes like 'non-HV repack' and 'convert your INSTALLED HV version'. content.text:
Your answers pin the target. Here is the closed-out diagnosis — **no code was changed**.

## Confirmed target vs. current behaviour

| Your intent | What the code does today | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| **Latest mode** — Metacritic-first, window controlled by `max_date` (or `max_pages` when `max_date: 0`) | Exactly that mechanism — but `max_date` is a **floor**, not a "latest" switch. The sweep starts at the top of the floor year and walks *down* page by page, resuming at a cursor, and only resets when the whole floor range is done. With `max_date: 202601`, `max_cycle_months: 1`, it is ~866 cached 2026 pages, ~16 pages per cycle: a slow crawl through the year, not "look at what's new". | **No concept of "only the newest N games"** — nothing stops after the first pages of the current month. `max_date` bounds how *old* it goes; it does not bound how *deep* it crawls within the window. |
| **Backlog mode** — walk a backlog, check each game exists on FitGirl/FreeGOG | Exists: sweep window → queue → verify → source lookup. | Works structurally, but the queue is a graveyard (1,555 pending, 1,534 below thresholds, 16,896 expired all-time) and the source lookup is blocked (below). |
| **Sort by critic/user score** | `sort_order` is **order only**, never a filter; and in `criticscore`/`userscore` there is no year dimension, so `max_date` is ignored there (logged each cycle). | If score should *filter*, it can only happen at detail verification — browse scores are Metacritic's internal metrics (~1168), not 0–100. |
| **Explicit mode switch** | No mode concept: behaviour is an emergent consequence of `max_date`, `max_pages`, `max_cycle_*` and `sort_order`. | Needs `mode: latest | backlog` (or equivalent) so intent is declarative. |
| **Filter before queueing** | Queue first, verify later. Pending is the holding pen, so below-threshold games occupy it for 30 days and are re-checked from cache every cycle ("1555 checked, 21 passed, 1534 kept"). | Verification must move **before** insertion, and below-threshold games must not be held. |

## The three defects that explain what you're seeing

**1. `hv` substring kills ~all deliveries (dominant).** `_title_contains_keywords` is a plain substring test over the whole FitGirl article body. Real page (Black Myth: Wukong) contains *"Only updated files for a new **non-HV** repack"* and *"convert your INSTALLED **HV** version"* — conversion-patch notes — so the token `hv` matches. Evidence: 7,821 skips on `hv` (+ 1,817 `emulator`, 771 `hypervisor`) across the log; **all 21 verified games** (Wukong, Metaphor, RE Requiem, Forza Horizon 6, Crimson Desert, JWE3…) blocked; **63 delivered vs 9,490 failed vs 16,896 expired** all-time. Your answer: keep the intent, fix the matching — so the fix must be whole-word plus negation-aware (`non-HV`, `without HV`), and/or scoped to the repack title + "Repack Features" rather than the full body.

**2. "Latest" is a slow crawl, not a look at what's new.** The 2026 listing is 866 cached pages deep; a cycle advances ~16 pages and mostly re-sees known slugs — *"3 of 800 collected games passed title/age filters"*. New releases appear on page 1 only, are picked up once, then dedupe permanently excludes them. So you see no new games even though new games *are* on page 1 every day.

**3. Old games arrive in bursts.** What escapes the keyword blocker is typically a 2024/2025 title queued weeks earlier that finally matched; the last delivery batch (28 on Nov 5) was FF XVI, Dragon Ball Sparking! Zero, Red Dead Redemption, Romancing SaGa 2 — all ~2024. Expiry waves (276 on Oct 30, 110 on Nov 1) explain the "no pattern" feeling.

## What needs changing (the change list, no code yet)

1. **Keyword matcher** — whole-word, negation-aware, and scoped to title + requirements/features; add a regression test using a real "non-HV repack" article.
2. **Explicit `mode`** — `latest` (shallow: newest pages of the window, e.g. first N pages / current month only, then stop) vs `backlog` (deep: cursor-driven sweep to the floor). Plus the existing `sort_order` applying to both.
3. **Filter before queueing** — queue only games that already pass detail thresholds; below-threshold games are dropped (or held ≤1–2 days), not 30. This alone drains the 1,555-strong queue.
4. **Window semantics made honest** — document/encode that `max_date` is a floor and add a depth control for latest mode (pages-per-cycle *and* a "stop after the newest month" rule), so "latest" cannot degenerate into a year-long crawl.
5. **Score filtering** — decide explicitly that critic/user score filters at verification, and that sort order only re-orders (which is what the code already does) — or make score mode bound the queue as well.

Nothing has been modified. If you want to proceed, the natural next step is a design spec for these five changes (then a fix chain) — say the word and I'll write it to `docs/agent/specs/`.

def _process_browse_games(
    browse_games: list[dict[str, Any]],
    platform: str,
    db: Database,
    thresholds: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    max_queue_days: int = 30,
    reject_title: list[str] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Evaluate browse-page games and insert qualifying ones into the pending queue.

    Browse listings from ``_parse_browse_page`` already include scores
    in their dict (``score`` = critic metascore, ``user_rating`` = user
    score).  Games that pass the thresholds are inserted into
    ``pending_games``.  Already-processed or already-pending games are
    skipped.

    Args:
        browse_games: List from ``_parse_browse_page``.
        platform: Target platform name.
        db: Database instance.
        thresholds: Dict with ``min_criticscore`` keys.
        max_queue_days: How many days to keep the game pending before expiry.
        reject_title: Titles matching any of these are skipped.

    Returns:
        Number of new pending games added.
    """
    known_slugs = db.get_known_slugs(source="metacritic")
    new_count = 0
    seen_slugs: set[str] = set()
    for game in browse_games:
        if not _is_game_eligible(game, db, thresholds, known_slugs=known_slugs):
            continue
        if _title_matches_reject(game.get("title", ""), reject_title):
            logger.debug("Skipping '{}' — matches reject_title", game.get("title", ""))
            continue

        reject_reason = _reject_by_browse_review_counts(
            game,
            min_critic_reviews=thresholds.get("min_criticscore_reviews", 0),
            min_user_reviews=thresholds.get("min_user_reviews", 0),
        )
        if reject_reason is not None:
            logger.debug(
                "Skipping '{}' — {}",
                game.get("title", ""),
                reject_reason,
            )
            continue

        g_slug = game.get("slug", "")
        g_title = game.get("title", "")

        # Skip duplicate slugs within this batch — the DB layer would
        # silently no-op, but we avoid the unnecessary roundtrip.
        if g_slug in seen_slugs:
            continue
        seen_slugs.add(g_slug)

        expires_at = _calculate_pending_expiry(max_queue_days)

        db.record_pending(
            slug=g_slug,
            game_title=g_title,
            platform=platform,
            metascore=float(game.get("score") or 0),
            metascore_reviews=game.get("critic_review_count"),
            user_score=float(game.get("user_rating") or 0),
            user_reviews=game.get("user_review_count"),
            release_date=game.get("release_date"),
            expires_at=expires_at,
        )
        new_count += 1
        logger.debug(
            "Added pending game: '{}' (slug: {}, expires {})",
            g_title,
            g_slug,
            expires_at,
        )

    return new_count

def _verify_pending_scores(
    db: Database,
    mc: MetacriticClient,
    platform: str,
    thresholds: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    cache_details_days: int = 7,
    max_verify: int = 50,
    reject_genre: list[str] | None = None,
    reject_title: list[str] | None = None,
    fitgirl_max_queue_days: int = 60,
    notifier: Any = None,
    cancel_event: CancelSignal | None = None,
    sort_order: Literal["new", "criticscore", "userscore"] | None = None,
) -> int:
    """Re-verify pending games' scores against the real Metacritic detail page.

    Browse-page Nuxt data does NOT carry standard 0\u2013100 metascores or
    0\u201310 user scores — the \"score\" fields are internal browse-only
    metrics.  Games whose detail-page scores fail the configured thresholds
    (or cannot be found at all on the detail page) are kept in the queue
    for re-verification on subsequent cycles.

    Games that pass the real-score check have their pending record updated
    with the correct scores from the detail page.

    Only the first *max_verify* games are checked per call; the rest
    remain pending for the next cycle.  This prevents a large pending
    queue (e.g. 2773 games) from generating thousands of sequential
    HTTP requests in a single cycle.

    Args:
        db: Database instance.
        mc: MetacriticClient instance.
        platform: Platform identifier (e.g. ``"pc"``).
        thresholds: Dict with score threshold keys.
        sort_order: Active browse sort order used to order the pending queue
            (see :meth:`Database.get_pending`).  ``None`` keeps the default
            database order.
        cache_details_days: TTL for the detail-page cache.
        max_verify: Maximum number of games to verify per cycle.
            Set to 0 to skip verification entirely.
        reject_genre: List of genre substrings to reject (case-insensitive).

            E.g. ``["RPG"]`` matches ``"Action RPG"``, ``"JRPG"``, etc.
        reject_title: List of title substrings to reject (case-insensitive).
            Games whose title contains any entry are removed immediately.
        fitgirl_max_queue_days: Passed through to _process_verify_result for
            expiry recalculation when scores pass.
        notifier: Optional Notifier instance. When provided and every lookup
            in the batch returns None, a scrape notification is sent.

    Returns the number of games removed.
    """
    if max_verify <= 0:
        return 0

    removed = 0
    pending = db.get_pending(platform=platform, sort_order=sort_order)
    total_pending = len(pending)

    # Collect the batch of games to check this cycle
    batch = list(pending[:max_verify])

    if not batch:
        return 0

    removed, any_success = _process_verify_batch(
        db,
        mc,
        platform,
        thresholds,
        batch,
        max_verify,
        total_pending,
        cache_details_days=cache_details_days,
        reject_genre=reject_genre,
        reject_title=reject_title,
        fitgirl_max_queue_days=fitgirl_max_queue_days,
        cancel_event=cancel_event,
    )

        _diagnose_and_notify_scrape(
            notifier,
            _check_scrape_health(),
            "Metacritic game detail lookup failed for all games",
        )

    return removed

content.text:
Explored. Key facts I now have: `_process_browse_games` applies only cheap filters (known-slug dedupe, `reject_title`, browse review counts) before inserting into `pending_games`; real score verification happens **afterwards** over the whole queue (`max_verify=len(pending)`, so all 1,555 are "checked" every cycle from cache); matching only touches rows with `score_checks_passed IS TRUE`; and the FitGirl keyword check is a plain substring test over the article body.

Question 1 — the architectural core:

options.description: Latest mode always starts at page 1 of the current window and scans only the first N pages, then stops. N is the existing `max_cycle_pages` (page mode) or a new depth setting in date mode. No per-year cursors are used, so every cycle re-reads exactly the newest releases and dedupe (known slugs) prevents re-queueing. Predictable: 'the newest N pages, every cycle'.

No cursors, no deep crawl, always the newest.

options.description: Verify the detail page at discovery time. Insert only games that pass now. Games that fail are simply not queued — and because latest mode re-reads the newest N pages every cycle (and unqueued slugs are not marked 'known'), they are re-evaluated on the next pass until they either pass or drop off the pages. Cleanest queue, but in backlog mode a dropped game is not revisited until the sweep wraps.

content.text:
All eight decisions are locked. Here is the design — five sections; tell me what to change.

## 1. Goal and scope

**The problem, restated from evidence:** deliveries stalled because every FitGirl match is rejected on `hv`/`emulator` found in boilerplate text (7,821 skips, all 21 verified games blocked, 63 deliveries ever); the queue holds 1,555 rows of which 1,534 can never pass (16,896 expired all-time); "latest" is a deep cursor crawl (866 pages of 2026 at 16 pages/cycle), not a look at what's new; and modes are implicit, so behaviour has no predictable pattern.

**Four changes, one spec, sequenced implementation:** (1) keyword matcher, (2) queue migration + verify-before-insert, (3) `mode: latest | backlog`, (4) docs. Discovery stays **Metacritic-first** — no source-first scan is being added.

---

## 2. Config surface

```yaml
review_sites:
  metacritic:
    platform_overrides:
      pc:
        mode: latest        # latest | backlog  (default backlog)
        max_pages: 10       # latest: depth = first 10 pages
                            # backlog: total sweep budget (today's meaning)
        max_date: 202609    # window floor, both modes (0 = no floor)
        max_cycle_months: 1 # backlog pace only (inert in latest)
        max_cycle_pages: 16 # page-mode backlog pace only (inert in latest)
        sort_order: new     # latest REQUIRES "new"; score sorts warn + scan "new"
```

- `mode` is validated as a Literal; default `backlog` preserves today's behaviour, so the migration only adds the key.
- Latest mode: scans **pages 1..N of the window every cycle, no cursors, no reset**; `max_pages` is the depth, and `max_pages: 0` is clamped to 10 with a warning (unbounded latest is just backlog).
- Backlog mode: exactly today's semantics (cursor sweep, `max_date` floor, pacing).
- Inert keys log once per cycle as they do now (`max_cycle_months ignored in latest mode`, etc.).

---

## 3. Discovery pipeline

**Mode resolution** — one predicate, one branch, no duplicated loops:

```
use_cursors = (mode == "backlog")
depth_pages = max_pages                                  # only read in latest
scan_order  = "new" if mode == "latest" else sort_order   # warn when coerced
```

Latest drives the existing year loop with `start_page = 1` each cycle and a hard stop at `depth_pages`; backlog keeps `get_last_scanned_page` / `set_last_scanned_page` and the drained/floor reset logic. Logging changes in latest from `Progress: N of 1000 pages` to `Latest scan: pages 1..N of <window>, M collected`.

**Verify-before-insert** (the chosen approach): inside `_process_browse_games`, each game surviving the cheap filters (known-slug dedupe, `reject_title`, browse review counts) gets a detail lookup via the existing `mc.lookup_game` — which already honours `game_detail_cache` for `cache_details_days`, so repeated cycles are cache hits, not fresh HTTP. `db.record_pending` is then called **only** when the scores pass; it writes the real scores and `score_checks_passed=True`. Games that fail, or have no scores yet, are not inserted — and because unqueued slugs are not marked "known", the next latest-mode pass re-evaluates them automatically.

Two rejected alternatives: a `state` column on `pending_games` (schema change, and the queue still fills with candidates between phases) and a separate `candidates` table (new table, duplicated dedupe logic).

---

## 4. Keyword matcher

`_check_reject_keywords` changes in two ways:

- **Scope:** extract the page `<title>` and the **"Repack Features"** block and match only there. Drop the "truncate at Backwards Compatibility" hack — on real pages it sits at char 2221 and the features block at 4914, so today's truncation discards the authoritative section while keeping the download-mirror boilerplate that causes the false positive.
- **Match rule:** whole-word, negation-aware. `\bhv\b` with a negation window — `non-HV repack`, `without HV`, `no HV support` do **not** match; `HV version`, `requires HV` do.

Measured effect: the Wukong page's two offending sentences (chars 476 and 1027) fall outside the scope entirely, so the game matches again; a genuine HV repack states it in Repack Features and is still rejected.

---

## 5. Queue migration, error handling, testing

- **One-time data migration** (guarded, idempotent, runs once on upgrade): `DELETE FROM pending_games WHERE score_checks_passed IS NOT TRUE`. 1,555 → 21 rows (the verified candidates, including the `hv`-blocked games that will deliver once §4 lands).
- **Error handling:** a detail lookup that fails (network/parse) must not silently drop a candidate — treat it like a failed verification for this cycle and retry next pass (that is what the detail cache + re-read already give us); a missing features block degrades to title-only matching (and logs at DEBUG, never blocks the match).
- **Testing:** unit tests for the matcher (table-driven: `non-HV`, `HV version`, `hypervisor`, missing block), for mode resolution (latest/best-mode matrix, inert-key logs, depth clamp), for verify-before-insert (pass → queued verified; fail → not queued; lookup failure → retried), and for the one-time migration (idempotent, verified rows preserved). Plus a README-accuracy test for the new `mode` row.
- **Out of scope:** source-first scanning of FitGirl/FreeGOG; changing `sort_order` from order-only to filtering; per-mode scheduling intervals; any change to `max_queue_days` semantics for verified rows.

Implementation stays for the next chain step.

def _fetch_fitgirl_page_content(url: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Fetch a FitGirl repack page and extract its <title> and <article> text.

    Returns ``(title, article_text)`` where both are ``None`` if the page
    could not be fetched or the tag is missing.  The title has HTML entities
    decoded (e.g. ``'`` → ``'``, ``"`` → ``"``).  The article
    text has HTML tags stripped (including link anchor text from ``<a>``
    elements to exclude download filenames from keyword scanning) and
    whitespace collapsed.

    Returns:
        A ``(title, article_text)`` tuple.
    """
    try:
        # Only fetch from FitGirl (uses self-signed cert — verify=False is intentional)
        if not url.startswith("https://fitgirl-repacks.site"):
            return None, None
        resp = requests.get(
            url,
            headers={"User-Agent": _USER_AGENT},
            timeout=_SITEMAP_TIMEOUT,
            verify=False,
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
    except requests.RequestException:
        return None, None

    html = resp.text
    # Extract <title> tag content
    title: str | None = None
    match = re.search(r"<title[^>]*>(.*?)</title>", html, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
    if match:
        title = unescape(match.group(1).strip())

    # Extract <article> text content (excludes sidebar, nav, comments)
    article_text: str | None = None
    article_match = re.search(r"<article[^>]*>(.*?)</article>", html, re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
